text:
Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia
messageText: It is a privilege to lead Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar, one of the national accolades and an outstanding institution of higher learning. NIT Jalandhar is ranked 55th in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF-2025), Band-Excellent in the Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA), and was recently ranked in the 301-350 range in the Times Higher Education (THE) Young University Rankings 2024. These accomplishments are the result of responsive leadership, dedication of the faculty and staff, and considerable efforts by students. More importantly, even during the unprecedented situation of the pandemic, the Institute continued to generate and disseminate knowledge. While cherishing the journey and milestones achieved so far, we must look forward and prepare ourselves for future challenges to propel this institution to even greater heights.
title: Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia

text:
Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia
In the coming years, our primary focus will be on implementing the New Education Policy (NEP) in its true spirit, fostering inter-disciplinary research, deepening industry-academia collaboration, exploring and developing new avenues of knowledge, and resource generation through knowledge transfer. The students spend a significant portion of their lives on campus. They join the Institute to make their dreams a reality. In a world where change is the only constant, the Institute provides its students a solid foundation for their careers. The Institute gives them the opportunity to integrate their minds, imaginations, and emotions in order to become capable of resolving public issues. The students have twofold responsibilities: one is to transform themselves, and the other is to address the complex problems faced by the society. It is my earnest appeal to students to make the best use of the time they spend at the Institute for their holistic transformation. The students must keep their curiosity alive and experiment new things.
title: Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia

text:
Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia
Our alumni are also passionately concerned about the progress of the Institute. I seek their ongoing support in the form of reverse mentoring by serving their Alma Mater with zeal and exuberance.Last but not least, as this Institute is named after Dr B R Ambedkar, let us recall his slogan, ‘educate, agitate, and organise’. Let us educate society so that it is capable of generating innumerable ideas for human welfare. Let these ideas of thesis and anti-thesis agitate or collide with one another, and eventually organise into a new synthesis, what Higher Education Institute stands for. I am hopeful and confident that with everyone's support and commitment, we will achieve new milestones with ever- rising benchmarks, help our youth in making their dreams a reality, and propel the Institute to new heights.

research profile:
Research Interests:
- Bioprocess Engineering, Enzyme Technology, Biochemical Engineering.
Brief Research Profile:
- The expeditious consumption of non-renewable energy resources has awakened the world to harvest the energy from renewable resources for sustainable growth and development. Bioprocessing is revolutionizing the industrial landscape by integrating innovative leverages of biological systems, such as microorganisms and enzymes, to produce goods in an environmentally friendly manner. Bioprocessing techniques, like fermentation and enzymatic reactions, operate under mild conditions, leading to energy savings and lower operational costs. One of the key advantages of bioprocessing is its ability to convert biomass into valuable products, such as biofuels, bioplastics, different value-added products including biopharmaceuticals, enzymes, animal feeds and human nutrients etc. via microbial applications. These bio-based products are not only biodegradable but also reduce our dependence on non-renewable resources. I have been studying extensively in the various aspects of bioprocessing technology for the manufacture of goods based on utilizing waste biomass resources, which are the potential source of pollution to the environment.
title: Dr Asim Kumar Jana - BT faculty

text:
Dr Asim Kumar Jana - BT faculty
I studied the bioconversion of high cellulose content biomass to fermentable sugars by fungal delignification pretreatment of lignocellulosic biomass and enzymatic saccharification. Conversion of agricultural wastes into fermentable sugars, could be used subsequently in biofuels, other feedstock chemicals production by fermentation process. I studied the conversion of agri-residues waste as substrate in SSF for laccase production. Fungal laccases have potentiality in different industrial fields due to its ability to catalyze the oxidation of a wide variety of substrates e.g. paper-pulp bleaching, synthetic dye decolorization, bioremediation, textile processing, biosensors, food and brewery industry and petrochemical industries. My studies also included conversion of waste frying oils into biosurfactant has been studied in batch and fed-batch process. Food and beverage industries throughout the world apply various natural and synthetic flavours for enhancement of taste of existing or development of new products. Immobilization of enzyme on magnetic nano particles for environmentally friendly production of fatty acid esters through the economical biocatalytic process has been studied.
title: Dr Asim Kumar Jana - BT faculty

text:
Dr Asim Kumar Jana - BT faculty
I have also studied earlier fungal decolorization of the textile azo dyes, production of biodegradable starch based blend films. My current research is production of lipase enzyme from the new isolates for the studies in applications towards detergent supplements, environment friendly production of biodiesel and emollient esters etc. The number students who have been associated with me are 12 nos. in Ph D, 14 nos. in M Tech contributing 80 international journal articles (74 SCIs).

research profile:
Research Interests:

Brief Research Profile:
- My research area, Tissue engineering, allows the repair or regeneration of cells, tissues, and organs which have lost their function due to disease, injury or congenital defects. This engineering approach in medicine offers remedy to existing problems through delivery of stem cells and bioactive molecules onto three dimensional (3D) artificial extracellular matrix (bio-scaffold) prepared from either natural or chemically synthesized biocompatible and biodegradable materials (biomaterials). It may be either metallic, polymeric, ceramic, or composite. The wide range of natural polymer and ceramic resources still to be unveiled as biomaterial for tissue engineering applications. My research area deals with the processing and modification of silk fibroin from Bombyx mori, double layered eggshell membrane, hair keratine, eggshell, crab shell, and adding more to the list for the development of bioscaffold. The fabrication of 3D scaffolds with macro/micro porous architecture with nanoscale biopolymers and bioceramics by solvent casting-particulate leaching and freeze-drying methods have been employed in my research, however, efforts are being made towards electrospinning and 3D organ printing.
title: Dr Mahesh Kumar Sah - BT faculty

text:
Dr Mahesh Kumar Sah - BT faculty
The developed promising bioscaffolds have been further studied with mesenchymal stem cells (stem cell research) derived from peripheral and umbilical cord blood for bone and cartilage tissue regeneration. The influence of introducing bioactive molecules (metal ions, molecules, nanomaterials) on the induction of stem cell proliferation and osteogenesis is key objective of my research. The nanotechnology is contributing remarkably towards my research for the development of biomaterials with nanoscale topography or fibres to induce the cell proliferation in a particular fashion and directs towards cell differentiation of interest. Many of these natural polymers and ceramic biomaterials also exhibit the affinity towards heavy metal ions and thus processed and modified eggshell membrane and hair keratin is deciphered for water treatment (environmental engineering). The treatment of polluted drinking water and wastewater from industries could be well treated for the removal of heavy metals with developed biopolymeric system.

text:
Dr Prangya Ranjan Rout - BT faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Prangya Ranjan Rout is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Biotechnology at Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar, India, and served as a Visiting Professor at University of Manitoba during 2023–24. He is also the Co-founder and Director of Fermibio Solutions Pvt. Ltd., a biotechnology startup focused on advanced gut microbiome research and its translational applications in human health. His research work integrates experimental biotechnology with process intelligence, and translational sustainability solutions, with particular emphasis on scalable bioprocesses. Dr. Rout has authored over 150 scholarly contributions, including 66 peer-reviewed journal articles, 1 international and 2 national granted patents, 5 published patents, 3 books, 35 book chapters, and numerous invited conference contributions at national and international levels. He has secured multi-crore external research funding from major funding agencies including DST, DBT, BIRAC, IC-IMPACTS, etc., for projects related to resource recovery, nutrient removal, sustainable treatment systems, and gut microbiome engineering.
title: Dr Prangya Ranjan Rout - BT faculty

He is a recipient of the prestigious Science and Engineering Research Board–SIRE Fellowship (2023–24) and has been recognized among the world’s top 2% scientists in the Stanford–Elsevier global citation ranking. His major recognitions include the Odisha Young Scientist Award (2017), Best Practice Oriented Paper Award from American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE), and multiple Outstanding Reviewer Awards from ASCE. Dr. Rout currently serves as Associate Editor of Environment, Development and Sustainability and as Editor / Editorial Board Member for several leading journals including Scientific Reports, Discover Applied Sciences, and Journal of Water Process Engineering. He is also actively engaged in editing scholarly books for leading international publishers including CRC Press, John Wiley & Sons, Elsevier, and ASCE. His current translational research focus includes biomanufacturing of sustainable biomaterials, applied microbiology, process intelligence, and bioprocess innovation platforms aligned with global sustainability goals.

Dr Manoj Kumar - BT faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Manoj Kumar is currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Biotechnology at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar, Punjab, India. He completed his Ph.D. in 2022 from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Guwahati, where his research focused on production of biogenic metal sulfide nanoparticles from wastewater and their potential applications. Dr. Kumar holds a B.Tech. in Biotechnology from the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Raipur and an M.Tech. in Biotechnology from IIT Guwahati. Following his doctoral studies, he pursued postdoctoral research at the University of Naples Federico II, Naples, Italy, where he primarily worked on energy recovery from waste streams. Dr. Kumar’s research interests lie at the intersection of biotechnology, environmental sustainability, and nanotechnology, with a focus on developing innovative solutions for wastewater treatment and resource recovery.

Dr Hemant S. Chore - CE faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Hemant Chore has been in the field of academics and research and development since 1994. He is working in the field of Structural Engineering including Concrete Technology, Soil- Structure Interaction (an interface problem of Structural and Geotechnical Engineering), Ground Improvement, Foundation Engineering, Transportation Geotechnics ; and Pavement Engineering (Analysis and Design). He has guided around 10 PhDs and more than 55 M.E./ M.Tech. candidates in the afore-mentioned diversified fields of Civil Engineering. He has got more than 75 journal publications in the journals indexed in Web of Science (SCI/SCIE/ESCI) and Scopus data base. Moreover, he has got more than 225 publications in the Conference Proceedings and several Book Chapters. He has several IPRs (Patents, Designs and Copy rights) to his credit. He is on the Editorial Board of the International Journals (Advances in Computational Design and Scientific Reports).

- The primary research focus is Wind Engineering, with emphasis on evaluating wind-induced loads on buildings and roof structures using both experimental and numerical approaches. The research integrates wind tunnel experimentation and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations to investigate wind pressure distribution, aerodynamic behaviour, and interference effects of surrounding structures. text:
Dr Arya Anuj Jee - CE faculty
- “Durability study of concrete under aggressive environment”, “Non-destructive testing of concrete structures”, “Microstructure study of concrete”, “Corrosion monitoring in reinforced concrete structures”, “Sustainable construction materials”
Brief Research Profile:
- I did my Ph.D. from the Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati specialized in the stream of Infrastructure Engineering and Management (Construction Materials). My doctoral research is primarily focused on the effect of mix parameters including the replacement of cement with supplementary cementitious materials, and exposure environment (simulated chloride and chloride-sulfate solutions) on chloride and sulfate-induced durability problems in reinforced concrete structures. The change in microstructure (by XRD, TGA and FESEM etc.) of concrete exposed to different exposure environments and its effect on durability performance (ingress of aggressive ions and corrosion of embedded steel) of reinforced concrete structure was also focused on in my doctoral research work. Furthermore, an attempted for developing the relationships between ingress and corrosion parameters were also made. I did my master's (M.Tech.) in 2013 from the Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati.
title: Dr Arya Anuj Jee - CE faculty

text:
Dr Arya Anuj Jee - CE faculty
My master's research was primarily focused on the effect of mix parameters including the replacement of cement with supplementary cementitious materials, heating temperature, and sulfate ion concentration on chloride ingress in concrete. The chloride ingress parameters were measured in terms of the chloride diffusion coefficient. In addition, my research interest lies in the following fields: 1. Mechanical, durability, and microstructure study of concrete 2. Non-destructive testing of concrete structures 3. Corrosion monitoring in reinforced concrete structures 4. Sustainable construction materials As mentioned in my research interest above, currently I am working in the research areas focused on the use of sustainable construction materials in civil engineering constructions and their durability performance against an aggressive environment. Today, most of the construction in civil engineering is reinforced concrete structures. Therefore, from the sustainability of the construction industry, it would be interesting to identify the durability performance of the reinforced concrete structures made with sustainable construction materials against an aggressive environment.

research profile:
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Shibayan Biswas focuses on the behaviour of soil–foundation systems under static and cyclic loading, with particular emphasis on infrastructure founded on marginal and heterogeneous soils. His work integrates analytical approaches, advanced numerical modelling, and probabilistic methods to develop rational and reliable design frameworks for geotechnical systems. His primary research interests include computational geomechanics, constitutive modelling of cyclic soil behaviour, geotechnical earthquake engineering, offshore foundation system and reliability-based analysis and optimization. A major thrust of his research addresses shallow and deep foundation systems, such as closely spaced footings, caisson foundations, and machine foundations, where soil-structure interaction and failure mechanisms govern critical performance. He has extensively studied the application of geosynthetics, including geogrids and geocells, for ground improvement to enhance bearing capacity, reduce settlement, and improve dynamic response. His research also covers liquefaction assessment and liquefaction-induced lateral spreading, with applications to bridge and waterfront structures. Additionally, he works on geophysical site characterization, particularly multichannel analysis of surface waves (MASW), to support subsurface profiling and seismic site response studies.

text:
Dr Shashikant Yadav - CEE faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Our research focuses on sustainable environmental engineering, with a particular emphasis on carbon capture in natural aquifers. We study the rates of CO₂ absorption in aqueous suspensions of selected minerals to evaluate their potential for mineral-based sequestration and to assess the speed and efficiency of capture. This work combines experimental investigations with theoretical, modelling, and computational approaches, developing transport-phenomena and reaction-kinetics models to simulate and optimize capture processes. Our broader expertise spans CO₂ sequestration, multiphase reactions, mineral carbonation, waste utilization, polymer and edible films, analytical/numerical/soft-computing modeling, environmental engineering, socio-economic assessments, and green energy technologies.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Jatinder Kumar Ratan is currently working as Associate Professor in Department of Chemical Engineering, and Associate Dean (Faculty Welfare) at Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar-144011 (India) - An Institute of National Importance of Government of India. He is a gold medalist in Master of Technology (Chemical Engineering), and holds a PhD degree in the field of photocatalysis. He has almost twenty years of research and teaching experience both at undergraduate and postgraduate level. His research areas are applied photocatalysis, pollution abatement, water treatment and computational fluid dynamics. During his academic career, he has published as many as 50 research articles in reputed journals, covering the contemporary developments in applied photocatalysis. He has almost 60 publications to his credit in national and international conferences. In addition, he has authored two books with reputed international publishers, besides three book chapters on different aspects of chemical engineering.
title: Dr Jatinder Kumar Ratan - CH faculty

text:
Dr Jatinder Kumar Ratan - CH faculty
He has been granted five IPRs (Three Patents; one Design; one Copyright), and two more patents are in pipeline as of now. He has one technology transfer to his credit for manufacture of air purifier, which was launched commercially in November, 2020. He is the recipient of 'Outstanding Young Chemical Engineer' award by the Indian Institute of Chemical Engineers (IIChE). He has been conferred with Best Teacher Award in the year 2020. He has served on various administrative positions at National Institute of Technology Jalandhar viz Associate Dean (Research & Consultancy), Associate Dean (Faculty Welfare), Deputy Chief Warden, Deputy Registrar (Academics) etc. He is on the editorial board of various Chemical and Environmental Engineering journals. He has also served as Guest Editor to Journal of Indian Chemical Society (Elsevier); Environment Technology & Innovations (Elsevier); Environment Science and Pollution Research (Springer); and Nanotechnology for Environmental Engineering (Springer) etc. He is currently working on two industry sponsored R&D projects on commercial applications of photocatalysts.
title: Dr Jatinder Kumar Ratan - CH faculty

He has been elected as President of Indian Chemical Society-North Branch in the year 2020. He is the founder Chairman of Society of Chemical, Bio and Environmental Engineering (CHEMBIOEN). He is an Elected Fellow of Indian Chemical Society (ICS), and Life Member of Indian Society of Technical Education (ISTE), Indian Institute of Chemical Engineers (IIChE), International Association of Engineers (IAENG), International Association of Advanced Materials (IAAM) and Catalyst Society of India (CSI).

text:
Dr Shashikant Yadav - CH faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Our research focuses on sustainable environmental engineering, with a particular emphasis on carbon capture in natural aquifers. We study the rates of CO₂ absorption in aqueous suspensions of selected minerals to evaluate their potential for mineral-based sequestration and to assess the speed and efficiency of capture. This work combines experimental investigations with theoretical, modelling, and computational approaches, developing transport-phenomena and reaction-kinetics models to simulate and optimize capture processes. Our broader expertise spans CO₂ sequestration, multiphase reactions, mineral carbonation, waste utilization, polymer and edible films, analytical/numerical/soft-computing modeling, environmental engineering, socio-economic assessments, and green energy technologies.

research profile:
Research Interests:
- Software Systems, Computer Networks and Information Security
Brief Research Profile:
- The research works of the Dr Harsh K Verma collectively contribute significantly to the security research area, focusing on domains such as wireless sensor networks (WSNs), cloud computing, data hiding, and cryptographic protocols. One of the research studies a lightweight and energy-efficient architecture for WSNs while considering physical layer impairments like jamming, fading, and interference, enhancing both performance and resilience. Another addressed secure cloud data storage by implementing ID-based cryptography and certificate-less signatures, thereby offering scalable, lightweight, and privacy-preserving authentication in cloud–IoT environments. Steganography-based data hiding schemes has also been developed using novel techniques like PVA and AMBTC to improve both secrecy and stego quality. In WSN security, a novel access control protocol has been proposed to defend against malicious attacks using a one-way hash function, optimizing power and memory consumption. An enhanced threshold proxy signature scheme using RSA was designed to resist conspiracy and forgery attacks, ensuring secure delegation.

Research Interests:

Brief Research Profile:
- It has been said that one of the primary traits of accomplishing any type of task is to start with the end goal in mind and accordingly work in order to achieve it. A lot of students practice this starting from childhood until they have the opportunity when the right time arrives. While my friends fondly talk about their dreams, I just want to be good in my chosen field of research. Real-time and embedded systems are moving from the traditional design paradigm to integration of multiple functionalities onto a single computing plat- form. Some of the functionalities are safety-critical and subject to certification. The rest of the functionalities are non-safety critical and do not need to be cer- tified. Designing efficient scheduling algorithms which can be used to meet the certification requirement is challenging because the requirements of both the system designers and certification authorities have to be met within the given time budgets.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Shveta Mahajan is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar. She earned her Ph.D. from the Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research (AcSIR) in 2018. Her research focuses on the application of imaging techniques, including visible imaging, X-ray imaging, and hyperspectral imaging (HSI), for assessing seed quality. She investigates the use of these methods to evaluate physical purity, viability, and vigor of various seeds, aiming to develop image analysis-based alternatives to traditional seed quality assessment techniques. Dr. Mahajan has contributed to several publications in her field. Notably, she co-authored the article "Machine vision based alternative testing approach for physical purity, viability and vigour testing of soybean seeds (Glycine max)," published in the Journal of Food Science and Technology in 2018. Throughout her career, Dr. Mahajan has received multiple honors and awards, including: First Prize for Best Poster Presentation in the Information and Communication Science & Technology section at the Indian Science Congress in 2015.

field: Computer Science and Engineering
clg: Uttar Pradesh Technical University
research profile:
Research Interests:
- Edge and Cloud Computing, Algorithmic Game Theory, Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning, WSN
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Sumit Kumar received his PhD in Edge Computing-enabled IoTs, focusing on solving critical issues in the allocation of edge computing resources to IoT and mobile application users for task offloading. He has utilized game-theoretic approaches to address this NP-hard problem of resource allocation, providing innovative solutions from various perspectives. His research aims to optimize the operating costs of edge servers while improving the quality of services and resource utilization. Following his PhD, Dr. Kumar expanded his work to investigate the allocation of mobile and IoT users to edge computing environments, particularly in cases of uneven user density. His work in this area addresses the challenges posed by bottleneck resources on multitenant edge servers, aiming to maximize resource utilization and improve user allocation efficiency. Recently, Dr. Kumar proposed a novel technique to accelerate the convergence of existing game-theoretic approaches developed by various researchers, enhancing the effectiveness of solutions in task offloading.

Dr Gopendra - CSE faculty
Given by: Transaction of Machine Learning Research

research profile:
Research Interests:
- Multimodal AI for Social Good: Emotion, Reasoning, and Responsible Intelligence
Brief Research Profile:
- My research lies at the intersection of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, and AI for Social Good, with a focus on building robust, interpretable, and socially-aware intelligent systems. My primary research interests include: Multimodal Learning and Reasoning Modeling and aligning heterogeneous modalities (text, image, emoji, and conversational context) for tasks such as sentiment analysis, emotion recognition, sarcasm detection, and meme understanding. Emotion, Intent, and Cognitive State Modeling Developing frameworks for fine-grained detection of emotions, intents, distress signals, and cognitive distortions in dialogues, with applications in mental health and empathetic AI systems. Multimodal Conversational AI Designing dialogue systems capable of context-aware, emotionally grounded, and knowledge-driven response generation, particularly in multilingual and code-mixed settings. AI for Social Good and Responsible AI Detecting and mitigating harmful content such as misogyny, cyber-harassment, and abusive memes, with an emphasis on fairness, bias reduction, and explainability. Explainable and Trustworthy AI Integrating reasoning and explanation generation (e.g., RAG-based and LLM-driven approaches) to improve transparency, interpretability, and user trust in AI systems.
title: Dr Gopendra - CSE faculty

research profile:
Research Interests:

Brief Research Profile:
- Biomedical Signal/Image Processing: Biomedical signal processing involves analyzing physiological data such as ECG, EEG, and EMG signals to aid in medical diagnosis and treatment. Techniques like filtering and Fourier transforms help in extracting meaningful information from noisy data. Biomedical image processing enhances and interprets medical images from modalities like MRI and CT scans, using techniques such as image enhancement and segmentation to improve diagnosis, treatment planning, and anatomical visualization. Microprocessors and Microcontrollers: Microprocessors are versatile CPUs found in personal computers and high-performance systems, executing a wide range of tasks using complex instruction sets. Microcontrollers, on the other hand, integrate a CPU, memory, and peripherals on a single chip to perform dedicated functions with low power consumption and cost. They are integral to consumer electronics, automotive systems, and industrial automation, where they manage specific tasks in embedded systems. Embedded Systems: Embedded systems are specialized computing systems designed to perform specific tasks within larger systems, often requiring real-time processing capabilities.
title: Dr B S Saini - ECE faculty

text:
Dr B S Saini - ECE faculty
They combine hardware components like microcontrollers and sensors with dedicated software to operate reliably and efficiently. Embedded systems are ubiquitous in modern technology, powering devices from smartphones and home appliances to automotive control units and medical devices.

text:
Dr Ramesh K Sunkaria - ECE faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Ramesh Kumar Sunkaria was born in Kot Khalsa, (Amritsar), on February 20, 1967. He received B.Tech. degree (In 1990) in Electronics Engineering from Department of Electronics Technology, Guru Nanak Dev University Amritsar, and M.Tech. degree (2004) with Honours Degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering from Guru Nanak Dev Engineering College, Ludhiana (Punjab Technical University, Jalandhar). He did his Ph.D. Degree from Electrical Engineering Department, Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee, Roorkee in June, 2010. He has service experience of more than 31 Years in Teaching and Research, Industry etc. till date. He worked as Engineer in CNC/WEX Department, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, Haridwar upto June 1994, where he was involved in 200 MW and 500 MW TG Sets projects. Thereafter he joined Indian Broadcasting (Engineers) Service, Govt. of India and worked as Assistant Director (Engineering) until August 1996. He has executed the installation of numerous Radio and TV projects all-over India, namely, VLPT Joginder Nagar, VLPT Ahjufort, VLPT Kalakot etc., LPT Abohar, VLPT Kalakot, VLPT Thanamandi, VLPT Budhal etc.
title: Dr Ramesh K Sunkaria - ECE faculty

text:
Dr Ramesh K Sunkaria - ECE faculty
He joined NIT Jalandhar in October, 2001. At present he is Associate Professor in Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering, Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar, where he has been teaching UG/PG courses related to Signal Processing and Communication Engineering. Presently, he is also serving his Second term as Head in the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering in the Institute since February 2023, before this he served as First term as Head, Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering during February 2019-February 2021. He played a leading role in initiating the research and development activities in Biomedical Signal and Image Processing and other areas of Digital Signal Processing Applications. His current research interests are in Bio-Electric Signal and Image processing, Filter Banks and Non-linear Heart Rate Variability Studies. He has 83 publications in reputed referred International Journals and 69 publications in referred International Conference proceedings. He has guided nine PhD Thesis till now and six PhD Thesis are under progress.

He has established Medical Imaging and Computational Modeling of Physiological Systems Research Laboratory, Biomedical Signal Processing and Telemedicine Laboratory, IoT Laboratory under AWaDH CPS in collaboration with IIT Ropar, 2024. Dr Sunkaria has been awarded Best Teacher Award at NIT Jalandhar during session 2018-19 and Appreciation for highest marks in APAR in 2019-2020. - Dr. Nitesh Kashyap is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar, specializing in antenna design, microwave engineering, and high-frequency electronics. His research focuses on circularly polarized antennas, metasurfaces, intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS), high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), and microwave hyperthermia systems for cancer treatment. His multidisciplinary approach integrates simulation, fabrication, and experimental validation, contributing to advancements in wireless communication, medical electronics, and high-frequency device engineering.

- Chandan Kumar Singh (Member, IEEE) is currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar (NIT Jalandhar), Punjab, India. He received the M.Tech. degree in Digital Communication from Netaji Subhas University of Technology (East Campus), Government of NCT of Delhi, India, in 2017, and the Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering, with a specialization in Wireless Communications, from the Indian Institute of Technology Indore, India, in 2023. Brief Research Profile:
- Biomedical Signal/Image Processing: Biomedical signal processing involves analyzing physiological data such as ECG, EEG, and EMG signals to aid in medical diagnosis and treatment. Techniques like filtering and Fourier transforms help in extracting meaningful information from noisy data. Biomedical image processing enhances and interprets medical images from modalities like MRI and CT scans, using techniques such as image enhancement and segmentation to improve diagnosis, treatment planning, and anatomical visualization. Microprocessors and Microcontrollers: Microprocessors are versatile CPUs found in personal computers and high-performance systems, executing a wide range of tasks using complex instruction sets. Microcontrollers, on the other hand, integrate a CPU, memory, and peripherals on a single chip to perform dedicated functions with low power consumption and cost. They are integral to consumer electronics, automotive systems, and industrial automation, where they manage specific tasks in embedded systems. Embedded Systems: Embedded systems are specialized computing systems designed to perform specific tasks within larger systems, often requiring real-time processing capabilities.

text:
Dr Gaurav Kumar - HM faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Gaurav Kumar serves as an Assistant Professor at Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar, India. He completed his post-doctoral research in Financial Data Analytics at University College Dublin (UCD), Ireland. He holds a Ph.D. from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur, and an MBA from the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), Delhi. His doctoral research focused on the liquidity of midcap stocks. He also earned an engineering degree in Computer Science from the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Allahabad. Prior to academia, he gained industry experience as an SAP ERP consultant at Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). He has received several awards and grants, including the UGC Junior Research Fellowship (JRF). His research has been presented at various international conferences, including those organized by the American Economic Association (USA), ICMA Center (London), Corvinus University (Hungary), La Trobe University (Melbourne, Australia), IIM Ahmedabad, IIT Madras, IIT Kharagpur, and IIT Kanpur.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Karan Jain earned his Ph.D. in June 2019 from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. His research focused on diagnosing and predicting heart conditions using mathematical models. Before completing his Ph.D., he started working as a Research Consultant on a project sponsored by Tata Consultancy Services. This project aimed to detect heart problems using non-invasive methods like pulse and heart sound signals. His role involved leading a team of researchers and mentoring students. Since December 2019, Dr. Jain has been a faculty member in the Department of Instrumentation and Control Engineering at the Dr. B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar. His research interests include using machine learning to analyze biomedical signals and improving medical devices for better healthcare and modeling of physiological systems and associated diseased conditions.

- Currently I am working in an area of fracture mechanics and fatigue crack growth investigation of friction stir welded joint of Aluminum alloy. research profile:
Research Interests:

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr Rajeev Verma is working as Assistant Professor, Industrial and Production Engineering Department at Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar, Jalandhar, Punjab, India. Dr Verma received his PhD and Masters in Engineering (ME) degrees from Production & Industrial Engineering Department of Punjab Engineering College (Deemed to be University), Chandigarh. During his doctoral research, he worked for the ‘Development and Evaluation of Mullite-Nickel Based Coatings using an unconventional coating technique Slurry Spray Technique’. The work yielded a good number of publications in renowned peer-reviewed journals, including one in the Journal of Thermal Spray Technology (https://doi.org/10.1007/s11666-016-0437-1). Till date, He has more than 11 years of industrial and teaching experience. Dr Verma has successfully authored and co-authored 1 Book, 10 Book Chapters, 34 papers in International Peer-reviewed Journals, 30 papers in International Conferences, and 6 papers in National Conferences. His current area of research includes surface engineering, thermal spray coating technology, laser surface texturing, superhydrophobic surfaces, CAE, and Taguchi methodology.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Rohit Mehra is currently serving as a Professor in the Department of Physics and Dean, Research and Consultancy at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar. With a prolific research career, Dr. Mehra has authored more than 200 SCI-indexed research papers published in reputed international journals. He has delivered invited talks across the globe, including in the USA, UK, Canada, Japan, Egypt, France, and Thailand, and has been actively involved in organising international conferences of high repute. An accomplished research supervisor, Dr Mehra has guided 19 PhD scholars, supervised over 50 postgraduate dissertations, and is currently supervising 06 PhD students. He serves as a reviewer for over 80 international journals in the field of Radiation Physics and Dosimetry. He is a member of the editorial boards of three international journals in this domain. Dr. Mehra maintains active international collaborations with the National Institute of Radiological Sciences (NIRS), Japan, particularly in inter-comparison exercises for radon and thoron measurements.

Brief Research Profile:
- My research focuses on the design and modification of functional materials, including transparent conducting oxides, perovskite stannates, chalcogenides, and complex oxide thin films, for electronic, optoelectronic, and spintronic applications. I study how doping, strain, and swift heavy ion irradiation influence their structural, electronic, optical, and magnetic properties. Key contributions include the development of high-mobility stannate films, studies on Ge₂Sb₂Te₅-based phase-change materials for memory and NIR applications, and investigations of room-temperature ferromagnetism in transition metal–doped oxides. Some of my work also includes corrosion resistance in NiCr/TiO₂-coated steels and quantum and orbital phenomena in LaNiO₃ and Ba(Fe₁₋ₓCoₓ)₂As₂ superconductors. Using advanced techniques such as X-ray absorption spectroscopy, XMCD, and transport studies, I aim to bridge fundamental physics with materials engineering for next-generation device applications.

Brief Research Profile:
- In the course of my research activity, along with my collaborators, we have developed chiral constituent quark model with configuration mixing which is very well received in literature and it seems to have received good deal of attention from the international community. Our work finds reference in the work of Dhillon and Morpurgo, P. Ha and L. Durand, Jian Liu, Jun He and Y.B. Dong whereas, Lang Yu, Xiao-Lin Chen, Wei-Zhen Deng and Shi-Lin Zhu have been following the model developed by us. Apart from this, I am also working on a problem which deals with the structure of the hadrons in terms of the light cone wave functions. We plan to study the tomographical picture of the hadrons using the light-from quark model. The complex internal structure of the hadrons can be investigated through various distributions providing information based on their variable dependence.

text:
Dr Praveen Malik - ITEP faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- • The Liquid Crystal (LC) Research Group is actively engaged in the development of advanced soft functional materials for next-generation technologies, including smart windows, flexible displays, and gas sensing devices. The group focuses on understanding and tailoring the structural, morphological, electro-optic, thermo-optic, and dielectric properties of liquid crystal mixtures and their nanocomposite systems to achieve enhanced performance and multifunctionality. Our research encompasses a wide range of liquid crystal systems such as Blue Phase Liquid Crystals, Polymer-Dispersed Liquid Crystals (PDLCs), and Polymer-Stabilized Liquid Crystals, where significant contributions have been made and widely reported. • In recent years, nanomaterial–liquid crystal composites incorporating quantum dots (QDs), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles have attracted considerable attention within the group due to their remarkable ability to tune electro-optical and dielectric responses and provide better control over host LC properties. In addition, photoalignment techniques for liquid crystal alignment are currently being explored to enable improved device fabrication and enhanced optical performance.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Vinod Ashokan is currently serving as an Associate Professor in the Department of Physics at NIT Jalandhar, Punjab, India, since August 2018. His research interests lie in theoretical condensed matter physics, particularly theoretical study of structural and dynamical properties of “correlated quantum many-particle systems” in low dimensions. He completed his B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Physics from the University of Mumbai in 2002 and 2004, respectively. He then pursued his Ph.D. in Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics from IIT Roorkee under the supervision of Prof. B. D. Indu, which he completed in 2011. Following his doctoral studies, Dr. Ashokan worked as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Texas A&M University for 4 Years from 2011 to 2015. During 2012 to 2015, he was also a Visiting Scientist at Université du Maine, CNRS, Le Mans, France. He has further enriched his research experience through visits to several prestigious international institutions, including NUS Singapore, NTT Basic Research Laboratory (Japan), FH Münster University (Germany), and Technische Universität Dresden (Germany).

He has supervised 1 Ph.D. scholar and 15 M.Sc. research projects students, and is currently guiding 4 Ph.D. students. In addition to his academic contributions, he has actively participated in various administrative roles at NIT Jalandhar, including Chairman (International Cell), Coordinator (CSS), Member of National Education Policy, Member of NBA accreditation etc. He is also a Life Member of several professional bodies, including the Indian Science Congress, Kolkata, Indian Physical Society Kolkata, and Indian Physics Association, Mumbai etc.

Brief Research Profile:
- During my PhD, I studied nano-electromechanical resonators (NEMS) operating at millikelvin temperatures (~50 mK). I gained extensive hands-on experience with low-temperature experimental platforms, particularly dilution refrigerators of base temperature ~50 mK, characterization and fabrications of low-dimensional nano-electromechanical devices. My current research centers on the study of quantum Otto cycles. I investigate the performance of symmetric quantum Otto cycles under various optimization criteria. More recently, I introduced asymmetry into the quantum Otto cycle and demonstrated improved performance compared to the symmetric case, highlighting the potential advantages of asymmetric cycle design in quantum thermal machines.

Brief Research Profile:
- I work in the field of theoretical nuclear physics and nuclear astrophysics, with a focus on nuclear reactions in stellar environments that address fundamental questions of element formation and stellar evolution. My research covers scattering, breakup, knockout, and transfer reactions, as well as indirect methods such as Coulomb dissociation, the Asymptotic Normalization Coefficient (ANC) method, and the Trojan Horse Method to investigate low-energy reactions of astrophysical importance. I received my Ph.D. from IIT Roorkee (2013) and subsequently carried out postdoctoral research as a Research Associate at Texas A&M University-Commerce, USA, and as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at Université Libre de Bruxelles, Belgium. I have published over 28 peer-reviewed journal articles and several conference papers, and have led or contributed to major research projects, including Indo-Japan collaborations, the Ramanujan Fellowship (ANRF-DST, India), and the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellowship. I have also been involved in successful experimental proposals at leading international facilities such as RIKEN, Japan.

text:
Dr Mohammad Zafar - ITEP faculty
Organisation: The Indian Society of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics (ISTAM)
research profile:
Research Interests:
- Quasilinear Systems of Partial Differential Equations; Hyperbolic Conservation Laws and Nonlinear Waves
Brief Research Profile:
- Nonlinear (or quasilinear) hyperbolic system of partial differential equations, unlike their linear counterparts, come to us in tremendous variety; each with its own difficulties and require special treatments for solutions. The familiar laws of superposition, reflection, and refraction, applicable for linear partial differential equations, cease to be valid in case of nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations. The main complexity in the nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations is the break down of solutions within a finite span of time due to blow up of their derivatives and consequently forbidding the existence of global classical solutions. A fascinating feature appears in nature due to the breaking of solutions, i.e., the appearance of shock waves across which the medium undergoes abrupt changes in velocity, pressure and temperature. In contrast to the linear partial differential equations where signals propagate along the characteristics, the characteristics can cross each other precipitating the onset of a shock for nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations.
title: Dr Mohammad Zafar - ITEP faculty

Dr Mohammad Zafar - ITEP faculty

research profile:
Research Interests:

Brief Research Profile:
- My research focuses on the development of numerical and machine learning-based methodologies for solving forward and inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). I work at the interface of scientific computing and deep learning, with particular emphasis on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and related operator-learning frameworks for approximating solutions of high-dimensional, nonlinear, and multi-scale PDEs under limited or noisy data regimes. My contributions include the design of physics-constrained loss formulations, adaptive training strategies, and hybrid optimization techniques to improve convergence, stability, and parameter identifiability in inverse problems. I am also engaged in deep learning approaches for time series forecasting, focusing on capturing complex temporal dependencies in scientific and real-world datasets. The overarching goal of my research is to develop robust, computationally efficient, and physically consistent algorithms that can bridge data-driven and model-based approaches, with applications in geophysical inversion, fluid dynamics, and emerging biomedical systems. research profile:
Research Interests:
- Matrix Theory, Operator Inequalities, and Spectral Graph Theory
Brief Research Profile:
- My research interests lie in Matrix Theory, Operator Inequalities, and Spectral Graph Theory. My work focuses on eigenvalue and matrix spread inequalities, central moments, positive linear maps, and inequalities for Hermitian and positive semidefinite matrices. I also investigate operator inequalities arising from convexity, including Jensen-type, Hermite–Hadamard-type, and related refinements. In Spectral Graph Theory, I study adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, and (A_{\alpha})-type matrices, with emphasis on spectral bounds, graph spreads, energy, degree-based invariants, and extremal problems. My research combines techniques from matrix analysis, operator theory, convexity, and combinatorics to develop sharper inequalities and spectral bounds for matrices, operators, graphs, and digraphs.

Dr Vipin Kumar - ITEP faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Broadly speaking, my main research interests lie in the field of applied mathematics with applications to control theory. Specifically, I am interested in studying the qualitative behaviour of the dynamical systems of both integer and fractional orders using the time scales approach. In addition, I am also interested in the analysis of the switched, hybrid, and impulsive dynamical systems. Recently, my research interests have expanded to include the study of the qualitative behaviour of coupled and complex systems, along with neural networks to solve differential equations. My research also involves impulsive optimal control theory with applications in epidemiology.

Dr Mohammad Zafar - MA faculty
Organisation: The Indian Society of Theoretical and Applied Mechanics (ISTAM)
research profile:
Research Interests:
- Quasilinear Systems of Partial Differential Equations; Hyperbolic Conservation Laws and Nonlinear Waves
Brief Research Profile:
- Nonlinear (or quasilinear) hyperbolic system of partial differential equations, unlike their linear counterparts, come to us in tremendous variety; each with its own difficulties and require special treatments for solutions. The familiar laws of superposition, reflection, and refraction, applicable for linear partial differential equations, cease to be valid in case of nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations. The main complexity in the nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations is the break down of solutions within a finite span of time due to blow up of their derivatives and consequently forbidding the existence of global classical solutions. A fascinating feature appears in nature due to the breaking of solutions, i.e., the appearance of shock waves across which the medium undergoes abrupt changes in velocity, pressure and temperature. In contrast to the linear partial differential equations where signals propagate along the characteristics, the characteristics can cross each other precipitating the onset of a shock for nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equations.
title: Dr Mohammad Zafar - MA faculty

Research Interests:

Brief Research Profile:
- My research interests lie in Matrix Theory, Operator Inequalities, and Spectral Graph Theory. My work focuses on eigenvalue and matrix spread inequalities, central moments, positive linear maps, and inequalities for Hermitian and positive semidefinite matrices. I also investigate operator inequalities arising from convexity, including Jensen-type, Hermite–Hadamard-type, and related refinements. In Spectral Graph Theory, I study adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, and (A_{\alpha})-type matrices, with emphasis on spectral bounds, graph spreads, energy, degree-based invariants, and extremal problems. My research combines techniques from matrix analysis, operator theory, convexity, and combinatorics to develop sharper inequalities and spectral bounds for matrices, operators, graphs, and digraphs.

research profile:
Research Interests:
- Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing, Time Series Forecasting ; Machine Learning
Brief Research Profile:
- My research focuses on the development of numerical and machine learning-based methodologies for solving forward and inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). I work at the interface of scientific computing and deep learning, with particular emphasis on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and related operator-learning frameworks for approximating solutions of high-dimensional, nonlinear, and multi-scale PDEs under limited or noisy data regimes. My contributions include the design of physics-constrained loss formulations, adaptive training strategies, and hybrid optimization techniques to improve convergence, stability, and parameter identifiability in inverse problems. I am also engaged in deep learning approaches for time series forecasting, focusing on capturing complex temporal dependencies in scientific and real-world datasets. The overarching goal of my research is to develop robust, computationally efficient, and physically consistent algorithms that can bridge data-driven and model-based approaches, with applications in geophysical inversion, fluid dynamics, and emerging biomedical systems. text:
Dr Vipin Kumar - MA faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Broadly speaking, my main research interests lie in the field of applied mathematics with applications to control theory. Specifically, I am interested in studying the qualitative behaviour of the dynamical systems of both integer and fractional orders using the time scales approach. In addition, I am also interested in the analysis of the switched, hybrid, and impulsive dynamical systems. Recently, my research interests have expanded to include the study of the qualitative behaviour of coupled and complex systems, along with neural networks to solve differential equations. My research also involves impulsive optimal control theory with applications in epidemiology.

text:
Dr Joseph Anand Vaz - ME faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Anand Vaz was born in Mangalore, India. He received the B.E. (Mech) degree from the College of Engineering Poona, University of Poona, in 1985, M.Tech and Ph.D from the Department of Mechanical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, in 1988 and 1996 respectively. He is a Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar since October 2007, and the Coordinator of the ISRO Space Technology Incubation Centre (S-TIC) at NIT Jalandhar. He was also the Head of the Department of Mechanical Engineering from 2009-2012, and also served as the Dean (Academic) till January 2017. Before coming to NIT Jalandhar, he was a Professor at the Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), India, since 1999, and was an Assistant Professor at the same institution from 1993 to 1999. At SLIET, he had also handled responsibilities as Dean (Academics), Dean (Planning & Research) and Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department and Workshop.
title: Dr Joseph Anand Vaz - ME faculty

text:
Dr Joseph Anand Vaz - ME faculty
He has also served with the Machine Tools division of M/s. Voltas Ltd., India, 1985-86, and with M/s. Sriram Diesels, Balanagar, Hyderabad, India, 1988. He has been an invited Professor to LAIL, Ecole Centrale de Lille, France, in 2015, 2014, 2012, 2010, 2007, 2002 and 2000. He was awarded a JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Foreign Researchers in Japan by the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS), and pursued research at the Department of Robotics, Ritsumeikan University, Japan, 2002-2004. He has been to the United States, France, Japan, Spain, UK, Israel, Italy and Malaysia for dissemination of research work. He has completed five sponsored research and consultancy projects and is currently supervising 3 PhD scholars. He has been a reviewer for the ASME Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement and Control, IEEE transactions on Robotics, Journal of the Franklin Institute, Mechanism and Machine Theory, IASTED International Journal of Modeling, Simulation and Control.
title: Dr Joseph Anand Vaz - ME faculty

text:
Dr Joseph Anand Vaz - ME faculty
He is a member of the ASME, IEEE, Life member of ISTE and The Association for Machines and Mechanisms (AMM). He had founded the ASME student section at NIT Jalandhar in 2011. He was chairman of NCDDM 2007 at SLIET Longowal, has delivered several keynote lectures, and has chaired several conference sessions both in India and abroad. He has coordinated and organized several MHRD/AICTE sponsored faculty development programmes on Mechatronics, Modeling and Simulation, etc. and two GIAN courses. His research interests are in System Dynamics and Control – especially using the unified approach of Bond Graph, Mechatronics, Robotics and Automation, Mechanisms and Machines, Simulation, understanding musculoskeletal actuation and systematic development of prosthetic devices for rehabilitation of hand impairment. His lectures on the Fundamentals of Mechatronics, Bond graph modeling, simulation and Control, Robotics, .. are available on YouTube. He is also very passionate about teaching and has designed many innovative lecture presentations with MATLAB based simulations, and developed several innovative experimental setups for the Mechatronics Lab.

- Dr. Rajan Kumar is currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar, Punjab, India. He holds a strong academic and research background in the field of Mechanical Engineering with expertise in thermal sciences, energy systems, and battery thermal management. Dr. Kumar received his B.Tech. degree in Mechanical Engineering from HPU Shimla, followed by M.Tech. in Thermal Engineering from NIT Jalandhar. He pursued his doctoral research (Ph.D.) from IIT Mandi, in the area of microfluidics, where his work primarily focused on laminar micro-convection of gas and liquid with variations in fluid properties under the supervision of Prof. Shripad P. Mahulikar. His academic training and research experience have enabled him to contribute significantly to the development of efficient energy systems. His research interests include thermal energy storage, renewable and non-conventional energy systems, energy efficiency in industrial applications, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).

Brief Research Profile:
- Prof. Tangellapalli Srinivas is an academic and researcher specializing in waste heat recovery, solar energy, thermal polygeneration, exergy optimization, and sustainable energy systems, with extensive experience in research, industry, teaching, academic leadership, technology development, and international collaboration. Prof. T. Srinivas is a Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar, Punjab, India. He previously served as a Professor at the CO₂ Research and Green Technologies Centre, School of Mechanical Engineering, Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), Vellore, Tamil Nadu. He received his Ph.D. from JNT University College of Engineering, Hyderabad, Telangana, in 2008 and served as a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Ontario Institute of Technology (UOIT), Canada, in 2010 and 2013. Prof. Srinivas has served as the Principal Investigator of research projects funded by CSIR, SERB, IMPRINT, DST, and SPARC. He also has industrial consulting experience in solar thermal energy and thermal systems. He holds nine granted patents and two copyrights.
title: Dr Srinivas Tangellapalli - ME faculty

text:
Dr Srinivas Tangellapalli - ME faculty
He has authored six books, edited three books, contributed 25 book chapters, and published more than 225 peer-reviewed journal and conference papers. He has supervised six Ph.D. scholars, 40 master's theses, and 50 undergraduate projects. In addition to his academic career, he has four years of industrial experience in the machine tool industry. He also serves on the editorial boards of Recent Innovations in Chemical Engineering and Applied Solar Energy (Springer). In recognition of his contributions to teaching and education, Prof. Srinivas received the Best Teacher Award at NIT Jalandhar in 2021. In 2023, he received the Innovative Teaching Award at the 2nd Leadership Convention on “World is One,” organized by the World Leadership Academy and Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT), Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Prof. Srinivas was also recognized among the career-long Top 2% of World Scientists in the Stanford University–Elsevier rankings in 2024 and 2025.

- Product Design and Innovation, Advanced Hybrid Manufacturing Processes and Technologies: Dieless Manufacturing, Additive Manufacturing; Computer Aided Design and Analysis: Topology Optimization, Biologically Inspired Design, Bio-CAD
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Parnika Shrivastava received her doctorate from IITDJM in the year 2019. Her prime area of research is Advanced Forming Operations preliminarily focusing on Single Point Incremental Forming technique. She has reported in-depth analysis of deformation mechanism and failure behavior of formed samples, with the help of microstructure and crystallographic texture analysis of formed sheets explaining the complex evolution of sheet during SPIF. Further, efforts have been made to evaluate process deformation characteristics such as dimensional accuracy, thickness distribution, true surface strain, von Mises stress and equivalent plastic strain, evolved at different stages of forming and different strain conditions. Her work culminated in increasing the efficiency of SPIF process in terms of improved formability, geometrical accuracy and surface finish. She holds expansive expertise in process optimization, CAD/CAM (Modelling and Tool Path Design Strategies), CAE (FEA based Numerical Modelling & Simulation) and microstructure & crystallographic texture analysis. In addition, extensive research has been done to characterize the surface roughness of the formed samples.

text:
Dr Harpreet Singh - ME faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Harpreet Singh research interests broadly encompass the advancement of precision machining processes, nano-finishing science and technology, green and additive manufacturing methods, microwave processing of metals and composites, polymer processing, and particulate metal composites (PMCs), along with material processing and characterization. He is among the first researchers in the world to propose and develop a pulse DC supply controlled and ultrasonic vibration–assisted electrochemical honing (ECH) machine. At present, he and his research group are pioneering a new era in nanofinishing science and technology through the CMMRAF process for biomedical applications the first method proposed for nanofinishing of complex geometries. His research group has made significant contributions to green manufacturing, particularly in the microwave heating of metals, alloys, and composites, aimed at establishing near-net-shape manufacturing possibilities. Furthermore, their studies on PMCs reinforced with graphite and aluminum oxide, as well as natural fiber composites, have provided valuable insights for advancements in the defense and gear industries.
title: Dr Harpreet Singh - ME faculty

text:
Dr Harpreet Singh - ME faculty
His group is also actively engaged in the additive manufacturing of lightweight, high-strength alloys for aerospace applications. With over 17 years of research and teaching experience at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, Dr. Singh has published more than 90 research papers in reputed international peer-reviewed journals and conferences in India and abroad, and holds two patents. He has successfully guided Ph.D. (Awarded: 04; Ongoing: 03), M.Tech (Awarded: 21; Ongoing: 01), and B.Tech (6-Month Internship Projects: Awarded: 46) students. He also serves as a reviewer for various government-funded projects and several leading international journals of repute. He has been recognized among the career-long Top 2% of World Scientists in surveys conducted by Stanford University in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Additionally, he has been a resource person and invited speaker at numerous national and international conferences, STTPs, and QIP programs.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Rohit Mehra is currently serving as a Professor in the Department of Physics and Dean, Research and Consultancy at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar. With a prolific research career, Dr. Mehra has authored more than 200 SCI-indexed research papers published in reputed international journals. He has delivered invited talks across the globe, including in the USA, UK, Canada, Japan, Egypt, France, and Thailand, and has been actively involved in organising international conferences of high repute. An accomplished research supervisor, Dr Mehra has guided 19 PhD scholars, supervised over 50 postgraduate dissertations, and is currently supervising 06 PhD students. He serves as a reviewer for over 80 international journals in the field of Radiation Physics and Dosimetry. He is a member of the editorial boards of three international journals in this domain. Dr. Mehra maintains active international collaborations with the National Institute of Radiological Sciences (NIRS), Japan, particularly in inter-comparison exercises for radon and thoron measurements.

Brief Research Profile:
- My research focuses on the design and modification of functional materials, including transparent conducting oxides, perovskite stannates, chalcogenides, and complex oxide thin films, for electronic, optoelectronic, and spintronic applications. I study how doping, strain, and swift heavy ion irradiation influence their structural, electronic, optical, and magnetic properties. Key contributions include the development of high-mobility stannate films, studies on Ge₂Sb₂Te₅-based phase-change materials for memory and NIR applications, and investigations of room-temperature ferromagnetism in transition metal–doped oxides. Some of my work also includes corrosion resistance in NiCr/TiO₂-coated steels and quantum and orbital phenomena in LaNiO₃ and Ba(Fe₁₋ₓCoₓ)₂As₂ superconductors. Using advanced techniques such as X-ray absorption spectroscopy, XMCD, and transport studies, I aim to bridge fundamental physics with materials engineering for next-generation device applications.

text:
Dr Praveen Malik - PH faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- • The Liquid Crystal (LC) Research Group is actively engaged in the development of advanced soft functional materials for next-generation technologies, including smart windows, flexible displays, and gas sensing devices. The group focuses on understanding and tailoring the structural, morphological, electro-optic, thermo-optic, and dielectric properties of liquid crystal mixtures and their nanocomposite systems to achieve enhanced performance and multifunctionality. Our research encompasses a wide range of liquid crystal systems such as Blue Phase Liquid Crystals, Polymer-Dispersed Liquid Crystals (PDLCs), and Polymer-Stabilized Liquid Crystals, where significant contributions have been made and widely reported. • In recent years, nanomaterial–liquid crystal composites incorporating quantum dots (QDs), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), metallic and metal-oxide nanoparticles have attracted considerable attention within the group due to their remarkable ability to tune electro-optical and dielectric responses and provide better control over host LC properties. In addition, photoalignment techniques for liquid crystal alignment are currently being explored to enable improved device fabrication and enhanced optical performance.

Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Vinod Ashokan is currently serving as an Associate Professor in the Department of Physics at NIT Jalandhar, Punjab, India, since August 2018. His research interests lie in theoretical condensed matter physics, particularly theoretical study of structural and dynamical properties of “correlated quantum many-particle systems” in low dimensions. He completed his B.Sc. and M.Sc. in Physics from the University of Mumbai in 2002 and 2004, respectively. He then pursued his Ph.D. in Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics from IIT Roorkee under the supervision of Prof. B. D. Indu, which he completed in 2011. Following his doctoral studies, Dr. Ashokan worked as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Texas A&M University for 4 Years from 2011 to 2015. During 2012 to 2015, he was also a Visiting Scientist at Université du Maine, CNRS, Le Mans, France. He has further enriched his research experience through visits to several prestigious international institutions, including NUS Singapore, NTT Basic Research Laboratory (Japan), FH Münster University (Germany), and Technische Universität Dresden (Germany).

He has supervised 1 Ph.D. scholar and 15 M.Sc. research projects students, and is currently guiding 4 Ph.D. students. In addition to his academic contributions, he has actively participated in various administrative roles at NIT Jalandhar, including Chairman (International Cell), Coordinator (CSS), Member of National Education Policy, Member of NBA accreditation etc. He is also a Life Member of several professional bodies, including the Indian Science Congress, Kolkata, Indian Physical Society Kolkata, and Indian Physics Association, Mumbai etc.

During his tenure at UGC-DAE CSR Indore, Dr. Kiran was an active team member in the development of low temperature (2-300K) and high magnetic field (0-8T) X-Ray Diffraction setup using Lab. source; a unique facility in the country. research profile:
Research Interests:
- theoretical nuclear physics, reactions with radioactive nuclei, Nuclear astrophysics, cosmology and few-body physics.
Brief Research Profile:
- I work in the field of theoretical nuclear physics and nuclear astrophysics, with a focus on nuclear reactions in stellar environments that address fundamental questions of element formation and stellar evolution. My research covers scattering, breakup, knockout, and transfer reactions, as well as indirect methods such as Coulomb dissociation, the Asymptotic Normalization Coefficient (ANC) method, and the Trojan Horse Method to investigate low-energy reactions of astrophysical importance. I received my Ph.D. from IIT Roorkee (2013) and subsequently carried out postdoctoral research as a Research Associate at Texas A&M University-Commerce, USA, and as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at Université Libre de Bruxelles, Belgium. I have published over 28 peer-reviewed journal articles and several conference papers, and have led or contributed to major research projects, including Indo-Japan collaborations, the Ramanujan Fellowship (ANRF-DST, India), and the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellowship. I have also been involved in successful experimental proposals at leading international facilities such as RIKEN, Japan.
title: Dr Shubhchintak - PH faculty

Dr Lalit Jajpura - TT faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr Lalit Jajpura, did his B.E. in Textile Chemistry from MLVTI, Bhilwara and MSc. Tech and Ph.D. Tech from ICT (formerly known as UDCT), Mumbai. He worked as assistant professor for 4 year at TIT&S bhiwani. Before joining to NIT Jalandhar in 2018, He served for 9.5 year in BPS Women University (State University, Haryana) in various capacity i.e. reader, associated professor and Professor. He has 24 years of academic and research experience. The major area of his research is chemical wet processing, functional finishing of textiles, micro encapsulations for controlled release applications, bioprocessing of textiles, self-cleaning textiles, natural extracts, dyes and polymeric applications to textiles, sustainable textiles and technical textiles.

text:
Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty
Brief Research Profile:
- Dr. Mukesh Bajya has been working on important projects related to developing lightweight, cost-effective soft body armour by using different high-performance materials and indigenous technologies with DRDO, and Reliance Industries Ltd project. He has developed a soft armour panel based on indigenous non-ballistic material (polycarbonate sheet) and technologies that give promising results in ballistic performance (product of DSM Dyneema® and Honeywell-Spectra®) to reduce behind blunt armour trauma. Furthermore, he has also developed armour panels based on shear-thickening fluid and indigenous high-performance material (dis-entangled polyethylene tape). Other techniques include surface treatment with nanomaterials, hybridization, cross-ply UD laminates of high-performance disentangled polyethylene tape, thermoplastic composites, 2D and 3D fabric for para-aramid and UHMWPE to improve the impact performance. He is also working on the simulation of high-velocity bullet impact on a soft armour panel (made from UD laminates of UHMWPE fiber and polycarbonate sheet) in LS-Dyna by using the material model MAT054.
title: Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty

text:
Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty
The research has resulted in Ten publications in reputed journals viz., Composite Part B: Engineering (2022, 183, 107721), Composite Structure (2021, 255, 112941), Applied Composite Material (2021, 28, 1089-1109), Composite Communication (2021, 188, 100984), Composite Part A, Journal of Impact Engineering, Journal of Nature fiber and Journal of Thermoplastic Composite Materials and three Indian patents filed and published, and two more research articles are ready to be submitted for publication in reputed journals. He has received five prestigious National awards during his Ph.D. work. Apart from his research work, he has also worked for Reliance Industries Ltd and Defence Research Development Organisation (DRDO) for new products development such as soft armour panel vests, cut resistance gloves, high-performance braided ropes from DPE tape, etc. Before pursuing his Ph.D. from IIT Delhi, he had a fourteen-month research experience as a Junior Research Fellow in ballistic testing and development of bullet resistance jackets, helmets, and bullet resistance glass at DRDO, Terminal Ballistic Laboratory, Chandigarh, India.
title: Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty

text:
Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty
Before joining DRDO, he had a ten-month experience in the textile spinning industry, which was very helpful in developing hybridized yarn for matrix and reinforcement for composite manufacturing. His credentials depict his sincere interest in high-performance materials, synthesis of smart materials such as shear thickening fluid, hybridized yarn, development of new high-performance fiber yarn, composites and computational modelling of high-performance material (UHMWPE laminates, para-aramid). He is also interested in synthesizing different high-performance polymers, foam for high-end applications, recycling fibre, yarn and fabric from PET bottles and optimizing the properties of the final product. He has developed and analyzed thermoplastic composite during his research for bullet resistance applications. He has prepared reinforcements such as woven fabric and laminates used during his research work using a lab-scale facility. He is well-versed in manufacturing, optimizing quality parameters and the intended inspection methods for validation of composites.
title: Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty

text:
Dr Mukesh Bajya - TT faculty
He is also well experienced in handling characterization and testing instruments, including dynamic impact testing, high-velocity impact testing, SEM, TEM, FTIR, TGA, DMA, UTM, optical microscope and rheometer. He is keen to work with your organization to explore his knowledge and skills. He has a hand on expertise on products such as DSM Dyneema SB51, SB71 and SB117 grades for soft body armour panels and HB grade for hard armour plate. He also has expertise with the product of Honeywell (Spectra). He has developed the hybrid configurations of soft armour panel as per Indian and NIJ standard requirements. He has ballistic testing experience (1.5 year) of bullet resistance jackets, helmets and bullet resistance glasses, etc. He has also worked on LS Dyna to simulate the real testing of soft armour panel by using MAT54 (cross-ply UD laminates). He has deeply analyzed the UHMWPE product of DSM Dyneema, Honeywell and indigenous material (DPE). He has analyzed the Dupont products (woven fabric) and UD laminates of para-aramid (Gold Flex).

title: 132nd Birth Anniversary of Bharat Ratna Dr B R Ambedkar (April 14, 2023)
desc: Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar has celebrated the 132nd Birth Anniversary of Bharat Rattan Dr B R Ambedkar. The function was started by the garland ceremony and floral tribute to the statue of Dr B R Ambedkar by the Director of the Institute Dr B K Kanaujia, Registrar Dr Ajay Bansal, Dean Student’s welfare Dr Anish Sachdeva and other dignitaries along with large number of students and staff. On this holy occasion several cultural programs were also performed by the students of the Institute. Director of the Institute Dr B K Kanaujia has also addressed the audience and put forward the vision of Dr B R Ambedkar with his efforts for making the constitution of India. Director NIT Jalandhar has also aware the gathering about thoughts and views of Dr B R Ambedkar about equality, socialism and empowerment of women. Professor Jagwinder Singh has also highlighted the great works done by the Dr Ambedkar for this nation.
title: 132nd Birth Anniversary of Bharat Ratna Dr B R Ambedkar (April 14, 2023)
