- 📌 Programme Outcomes (POs)
- PO1: Engineering Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
- PO2: Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyse complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences and engineering sciences.
- PO3: Design/Development of Solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
- PO4: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions for complex problems.
- PO5: Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

- PO8: Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.
- PO9: Individual and Team Work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

dept ph description
description: The Department of Physics started in 1989 at the erstwhile REC, Jalandhar. Originally oriented towards teaching undergraduate (B.Tech.) students, the department has come a long way since – today the department in addition runs M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs. The department strives to emerge as a premier centre of Physics education and research across the country. Our research is organized within the general areas of Condensed Matter Physics, High Energy Physics, Nuclear Physics and Plasma Physics. We have an even split of theoreticians and experimentalists, with experimental research in Radiation Physics, Thin Films, Liquid Crystals and theoretical research in Laser-Plasma Interactions, High Energy Physics, Condensed Matter Physics and Nuclear Physics.

position: Head of the Department
message: Physics is one of the basic scientific discipline that helps us to understand and organize the universe. The department of Physics has been established in 1989 with the sole aim of providing fundamental and advanced knowledge as well as to encourage students to pursue interdisciplinary research. Department has highly experienced, qualified, skilled and motivated professors who are always eager to disseminate theoretical as well as experimental knowledge amongst the students. The department has state of the art building, well equipped research labs, M.Sc & B.Tech labs and ICT based class rooms. The major emphasis is always on following best teaching and learning practices in the department. Physical science society (PSS) of the department organise different curricular and extracurricular activities among the students in the institute. We have highly motivated research scholars in the fields of high energy physics, quantum physics, plasma physics, liquid crystal physics, nuclear physics, material science, condensed matter physics etc. Students of the department join highly reputed institutes and companies after completion of course.

Department of Physics, NIT Jalandhar in collaboration with Technology Applications Service (TAS), New Delhi organized a workshop on Vacuum, Plasma and Thin Film Deposition/Processing Technologies from 20-11-2023 to 22-11-2023. This workshop was attended by 40 students (including MSc and PhD) of the department.
desc: Department of Physics, NIT Jalandhar in collaboration with Technology Applications Service (TAS), New Delhi organized a workshop on Vacuum, Plasma and Thin Film Deposition/Processing Technologies from 20-11-2023 to 22-11-2023. This workshop was attended by 40 students (including MSc and PhD) of the department. Dr R K Garg, Scientist from TAS demonstrated various experiments to the participants. All the participants were imparted hands-on training for Plasma characterisation, Paschen curve and deposition of thin film via DC magnetron sputtering & Thermal evaporation method. In this workshop, strong emphasis was laid on the applications of vacuum and plasma medium formation. During the interaction session with Prof. Arvinder Singh (Convener of the workshop) the participants informed that they really enjoyed the workshop. Participation certificates were given to all the students on the last day.

Many Many Congatulations to 𝐃𝐫. 𝐇𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐞𝐞𝐧 𝐃𝐚𝐡𝐢𝐲𝐚, 𝐀𝐬𝐬𝐨𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐟𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐨𝐫 for being awarded the prestigious Science and Engineering Research Board (𝐒𝐄𝐑𝐁)’s POWER Fellowship. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐎𝐩𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐖𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐧 𝐢𝐧 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐡 (POWER) Fellowship has been instituted by SERB to identify and reward excellent women researchers in Indian academic institutions and R&D laboratories, holding Ph.D. degree in any branch of science and engineering and is an initiative for empowering women researchers. It recognizes outstanding women researchers and innovators in India, in various areas of specialization. The award consists of a monthly fellowship amount and a research grant for a period of three years. Working in the area of theoretical high energy physics, Dr. Harleen Dahiya's group studies problems to understand the three-dimensional mapping of the quark and gluon distributions in the hadron which will be measured in Jefferson Lab and Electron Ion Collider in USA. For this, Dr. Dahiya’s group uses methods of light-front quantum field theory approach. The SERB-POWER fellowship to Dr. Dahiya will enable research on understanding the origin of the hadron mass is an important and fundamental question, related to our understanding of the origin of mass in the visible universe. Many Many congratulations to 𝗗𝗿. 𝗩𝗶𝗻𝗼𝗱 𝗔𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗸𝗮𝗻, Assistant Professor department of physics for being awarded the Science and Engineering Research Board (𝐒𝐄𝐑𝐁)-Core Research Grant. The scheme provides core research support to active researchers and eminent scientist to undertake research and development in the frontier areas of Science and Engineering. The award consists of a monthly fellowship for JRF for the period of three years and cost to establish high performance computing facility in the department. 𝗗𝗿. 𝗩𝗶𝗻𝗼𝗱 𝗔𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗸𝗮𝗻's area of research interest is in theoretical condensed matter physics; particularly, quantum liquids and strongly correlated electron systems. The project entitled “𝗦𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗰𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗹𝘆 𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗻𝘁𝘂𝗺 𝗙𝗹𝘂𝗶𝗱𝘀” investigate the correlation effects and ground state properties of quasi-one-dimensional quantum materials. Attempts will also be made to find properties of Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid parameters of these systems. Planned collaboration for the proposed work are with the 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘆, 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗞𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗱𝗼𝗺, 𝗠𝘂𝗲𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗼𝗳 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗱 𝗦𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲𝘀, 𝗚𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗣𝗮𝗻𝗷𝗮𝗯 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗴𝗮𝗿𝗵. 𝗗𝗿. 𝗩𝗶𝗻𝗼𝗱 𝗔𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗸𝗮𝗻 owes this achievement to 𝗗𝗿 𝗕.𝗥. 𝗔𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱𝗸𝗮𝗿 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗝𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗵𝗮𝗿 and his research group.

𝗕 𝗥 𝗔𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱𝗸𝗮𝗿 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗝𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗵𝗮𝗿, organised the Annual Sports meet on 17th February 2024. The event took place in the main ground and gymnasium hall. The mega event commenced with Nisha Chahal, Head of PSS, announcing the arrival of the respected 𝗗𝗿. 𝗩𝗶𝗻𝗼𝗱 𝗔𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗸𝗮𝗻 inaugurated the event by sharing a few words about how the sports play a vital role in the academic life and holistic development of an individual. M.Sc. students Lakshya, Jay, Sachin, Sameer, Ashish Dubey, Dewesh and Phd scholars Abhishek, Dhananjay Singh, Nisha Chahal, Shubham Sharma, Satyajit Puhan, Chetan Prakash Saini, Manoj, Vidit Gangwar, Cheshta and Neha also played an integral part in making the event a successful one. The sports day marked it's beginning by the 𝗖𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵. The first match was between MSc 1st year and MSc 2nd year, M.Sc. 2nd year won the match.

title: SERB-CORE Research Grant is awarded to 𝗗𝗿 𝗔𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗞𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗿
desc: On behalf of PSS, we congratulate 𝗗𝗿 𝗔𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗞𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗿, Associate Professor, Department of Physics for being awarded the Science and Engineering Research Board (𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗕)-Core Research Grant(𝗖𝗥𝗚).The CRG scheme of SERB provides core research support to active researchers to undertake research and development in the frontier areas of Science and Engineering. The award consists of monthly fellowship of JRF for three years. 𝗗𝗿 𝗔𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗞𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗿's research group studies the properties of exotic matter such as quark matter and hadronic matter as well neutron stars using the effective models of QCD.The research project entitled "𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗘𝗾𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗲 (𝗘𝗢𝗦) 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘀𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗶𝗰 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝘁𝗮 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿". The sanctioned research project aimed to investigate the impact of Delta resonance baryons along with hyperons and nucleons on the EoS and hence, the mass-radius relations, tidal deformability etc. with and without finite magnetic field. 𝗗𝗿 𝗔𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗞𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗿 owes this achievement to 𝗗𝗿 𝗕 𝗥 𝗔𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱𝗸𝗮𝗿 𝗡𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗶𝘁𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗝𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗵𝗮𝗿 and his research group

text:
dept tt description
description: The Department of Textile Technology has its existence since the inception of the Institute, National Institute of Technology Jalandhar, formerly known as Regional Engineering College. Since 1989, the department is steadily progressing to new heights and considering its latest developments and achievements, the days are not far when it will stand in parallel with other national institutions offering education on textile and allied fields specifically, fibres, polymers, and technical textiles. The Department offers the education in various fields of textiles through UG, PG, and PhD program, where in addition to regular teaching, UG students may opt for interns ranging from 4 to 8 weeks, which benefit them with exposure to industrial culture. The team of brilliant and extraordinary 15 faculty members of the department, honored with several national and international awards are working tirelessly in elevating the department to new heights, and the present international conference, third in series, is the live example of the same.
title: dept tt description

text:
dept tt description
Several prestigious awards like Lifetime Achievement Award by Venus International Chennai, Outstanding Paper Presentation Award by Manchester, UK, Wall of Fame Award by ULEKTZ, Prof. Indira Parikh 50 Women in Education Leaders Award by World Education Congress are in the name of faculty members of the department. Faculty members have also been distinguished as associate editor and member of editorial board of reputed journals in the domain of textile. The faculty members have conducted several short-term-courses (STC), self-sponsored and GIAN course related to various domains of textile including technical textile. Besides high quality teaching, faculty members are actively involved in research activities related to filtration, medical textile, sewing threads, seam characterization, fabric structure- property relationship, fluid and heat flow through textile structures, fibre reinforced composites, nanocomposites, functional textiles, and sustainable chemical processing of textiles.
title: dept tt description

text:
dept tt description
Development of open weave geo-meshes using recycled wool, value addition of pashmina guard hair, optimization of pulse cleaning parameters for achieving high level performance of filter media, design and development of fabric wet abrasion tester, studies on air ventilation in central air conditioning, and study of water cycle and efforts towards zero discharge, are few of the research works pursued by the department, which are highly valued and appreciated. It is noteworthy to mention that the department has received several financial research supports from government agencies like Punjab State Council for Science and Technology, National Technical Textile Mission, Khadi and Village Industries Commission, India Austria Joint research project, DST, CSIR, and industries like Davinder Sandhu Impex Pvt. Ltd. Ludhiana, and JCT Ltd. Phagwara.
title: dept tt description

text:
dept tt description
As a result, 10-patents (including granted, filed and under examination), 4-technology transfer, 100-research publications, 44-papers in national and international conference proceeding, and 10-book chapters are rewarding the high quality research, which has been facilitated by the excellent research facilities and infrastructure of department and institute, including excellent library facility. The department has also received several industrial consultancy projects and is one of the best approaching educational institute for textile industries of Punjab. In addition to industrial collaborations, the department is actively involved in MoUs with textile industries and textile research institute. MoUs with Vardhman and WRA are the significant achievements in this direction. Each year on an average 100 textile technocrats are transforming into an alumni of the department through UG, PG, and PhD programs, and these technocrats join the reputed textile industries like Vardhman, Reliance, Trident, Raymond, Arvind, Welspun, Infiiloom, Himatsingka, Jindal, Sportking, Gimatex, to name a few, where many of the undergraduates pursue the interns as well.
title: dept tt description

text:
dept tt description
It is of great privilege for the department that many of the alumni are now the executive, deputy and managing director at reputed national and international platforms. The high capability of graduating students can also be witnessed from their successful placements in IT and other allied industries with handsome packages. Considering the achievements and milestones achieved so far, department is looking forward to expanding its teaching and research domains by revising the exiting curriculum and improving the research infrastructure through research grants by submission of research proposals. The revised curriculum is majorly focusing on technical textiles where the department is incorporating courses like technical textile, geotextile, and industrial textile in the revised curriculum of the UG and PG. This is also in correlation of strengthening the vision of GOI, specifically in the domain of technical textiles.
title: dept tt description

text:
dept tt description
Further the department is dedicating his efforts to develop research facilities related to development of advanced textile materials constituting various synthetic and natural polymers and fibres, and textiles structures such as woven, knitted, braided, and nonwoven through submission of research proposals to various national schemes like NTTM, SRG, CRG, and SERB. The members of the departments are highly confident that, department will very soon progress to advanced remarkable heights, which will be an inspiration and motivation to all.
department: tt
title: dept tt description

message: Welcome to the Department of Textile Technology, Dr B R Ambedkar NIT Jalandhar. The Department of Textile Technology is the only department among 31 NITs that offers programs as B.Tech. (Textile Technology), M. Tech. (Textile Engineering and Management), PhD in all areas of Textile Technology. We have a dedicated team of 17 faculty members who have been honoured with several national and international awards and are working tirelessly in elevating the department to newer heights. Besides high-quality teaching, faculty members are actively involved in research activities related to Aerosol Filtration, Wound Care Materials, Healthcare Textiles, Nonwovens and Sewing Threads. Some of the recent products and technologies developed include Development of easy breathe facemask, open weave geo-meshes using recycled wool, value addition of pashmina guard hair, Bedsheet cum Patient Shifting Device, Design of Transmissivity Tester for Geotextiles, Development of Test Rigs for Assessment of Industrial Filter Media, design and development of fabric wet abrasion tester and Development of Tensile Impact Testing Machine.
title: Dr Lalit Jajpura

text:
Dr Lalit Jajpura
Further, IPRs related to Apparatus for Testing Cleanable Filter Media and Bedsheet cum Patient Shifting Device have been granted recently. The Department has more than 700-research publications in national and international journals of repute, 40-book chapters and 07 patents/IPR to its credit. Being one of the best approaching educational institute for textile and sports industries of Punjab, the department has received many industrial consultancy projects and several research grants from various government agencies. I am proud of the ways that we as a department work individually and collectively to generate research that matters, and to produce and share knowledge that enables our students to effectively engage society as competent and engaged global citizens, as well as successful and fulfilled professionals.

description: The International Students Cell (ISC) at NIT Jalandhar (NITJ) primarily focuses on managing the admission process for international students. Its key roles in admissions include: 1. Admission Process The ISC is responsible for overseeing the admission process for international students applying to various undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs at NITJ. It provides guidance and assistance in completing application forms, submitting necessary documents, and ensuring compliance with admission requirements. 2. Eligibility and Documentation The cell verifies the eligibility of applicants from different countries, ensuring they meet the academic and language proficiency standards set by the institution. 3. Admission Counseling The ISC provides counseling services for international students regarding program selection, course structure, and career prospects. It helps students understand the various academic programs offered at NITJ, including information on scholarships and financial assistance available to international students. 4. Coordination with Regulatory Bodies ISC ensures that all admission processes comply with the guidelines set by the Government of India , Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) , and other regulatory bodies.
title: International Student Cell

text:
International Student Cell
It coordinates with various agencies, including the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) , DASA , and SMA , for admissions under specific scholarship programs. 5. Pre-Arrival Guidance Before the students arrive at NITJ, the ISC provides pre-arrival information and assistance, helping them prepare for life in India. This includes sharing details on accommodation, travel, health insurance, and other essential information. 6. Post-Admission Support Once students are admitted, the ISC continues to support them through orientation programs, guiding them in their academic and personal journey at NITJ. It assists with settling into the campus, helping international students navigate their new environment. In summary, the International Students Cell at NIT Jalandhar primarily facilitates the admission process for international students by handling applications, documentation, and post-admission support, ensuring that the students can successfully enroll and integrate into the academic environment at NITJ. text:
Academic System
title1: Academic System
title2: Academic System
desc: Academic System (The information regarding Academic system in this website is for information only. The relevant regulations as approved by institute senate from time to time will be applicable to students.) The academic system at NIT, Jalandhar is framed on a credit based semester examination system. The credit system envisages a continuous evaluation of student’s performance, and provides flexibility for academic progress based on individual ability and convenience, subject to the constraint of the minimum requirements for continuation of the academic programme.The students are awarded a letter grade from the prescribed grading system in each course registered by them. For each pass grade, the students accumulate the course credits as earned credits. The academic performance of the students is indicated in terms of the number of credits that he/she earns and the weighted grade point average. A specified minimum number of credits should be acquired on semester or session basis in order to qualify for continuation in the academic programme and for the award of degree.
title: Academic System

text:
Academic System
Credits Each lecture/tutorial of one hour duration per week in a semester is assigned one credit. Each laboratory hour per week in asemester is assigned half credit. However, some courses are preparatory in nature and have half the credit weightage of a normal course. The courses without credit are termed as noncredit (NC) courses. Grades In a grading system, the evaluation in terms of marks is replaced by the award of letter grades.
title: Academic System

text:
Academic System
The structure and guidelines for the award of grades is given below: Structure of Grading System Grade Points Description of performance Recommended Cut off marks* S 10 Outstanding 90 A 09 Excellent 80 B 08 Very Good 70 C 07 Good 60 D 06 Average 50 E* 05* Marginal 40 I - Incomplete - U - Unsuccessful - W - Withheld due to shortage of attendance or withdrawal - NP - AuditPass - NF - Audit Fail - * Subject to confirmation based on standard deviation, if the sample size is greater than 20, and is flexible to the recommended of the individual course coordinator with proper justification. However minimum marks to assign a pass grade must be 40 for all academic programmes run in the Institute. *with effect from 2012 batch as per Senate decision in its 21st meeting The grades will be awarded to a student in each registered course including a laboratory course, based on his/her performance evaluated through a prescribed scheme of evaluation.
title: Academic System

text:
Academic System
The credits for the courses in which a student has obtained “E” (minimum passing grade for a course) or a higher grade will be considered as credits earned by him/her. In addition, the course in which a B Tech student to get NP grade, will also count towards his/her earned credits but to the maximum extent of 8 credits. Any course in which a student has obtained “W” or “NF” grade will not be counted towards his/her earned credits. In case of other (elective) courses in which U or W grade has been obtained, the student may take the same course or any other course from the same category when it is offered next. Further, “U” grade secured in any course stays permanently on the grade card. The weightage of these grades is not counted in the calculation of the SGPA and CGPA (Please refer for information above) An “I” grade denotes incomplete performance in any course due to absence at the end of semester.
title: Academic System

text:
Academic System
Upon completion of all course requirements, the “I” grade is replaced by a regular grade.The grades NP and NF are awarded in a course that the student opts to audit. Audit applications are allowed during the first four weeks of a semester. The audit pass (NP) grade is awarded if a minimum “E” grade is obtained in the course and attendance is above 75% in the classes. If either of these requirements is not fulfilled, the audit fail (NF) grade is awarded. In courses, where NP grade is obtained, the corresponding course credits are counted towards earned credits. The grades obtained in an audit course are not considered in the calculation of SGPA or CGPA. A “W” grade is awarded in a course where the student has opted to withdraw from the course.
title: Academic System

text:
Academic System
Withdrawal from a course is permitted until one week after the class test-I. Grade Point Averages The performance of a student will be evaluated in terms of two indices, viz., the Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) which is the Grade Point Average for a semester and Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) which is the Grade Point Average for all the completed semesters at any point of time. The SGPA is calculated on the basis of grades obtained in all courses, except audit courses, registered for in the semester. The CGPA is calculated on the basis of all pass grades, except audit courses, obtained in all completed semesters. Rules and Regulations for B.Tech Programmes
title: Academic System

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
title1: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
title2: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
desc: NIT Jalandhar IT infrastructure usage Policy NIT Jalandhar endeavors to provide all faculty, students, and staff with a modern, fully networked computing and IT environment for academic use. Users of NITJ computing, networking, and IT facilities are expected to abide by the following rules, which are intended to preserve the utility and flexibility of the system, protect the privacy and work of students and faculty, and preserve our right to access the international networks to which the system is connected. The IT Infrastructure Usage Policy applies to all Students, Faculty, Staff, Researchers, Alumni, Outsourced Staff, Visitors, etc., in short to all Users of IT Computing Services.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
Faculty, staff, students and other Users with authorized accounts may use the computing and IT facilities for academic purposes, official Institute business, and for personal purposes so long as such use does not violate any law, Institute policy or IT act of the Government of India. does not interfere with the performance of Institute duties or work of an academic nature (as judged by the NIT, Director). does not result in commercial gain or private profit other than that allowed by the Institute. Users are expected to respect the privacy of other users, and they may not allow any other person to use their password or share their account. It is the users' responsibility to maintain the confidentiality of their login credentials and protect their accounts from unauthorized use by changing passwords periodically and using passwords that are not easily guessed. Sharing of passwords for any purpose whatsoever is strictly prohibited.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
Any attempt to circumvent system security, guess others’ passwords, or in any way gain unauthorized access to local or network resources is forbidden. Users may not use another person's computing account, attempt to forge an account identity, or use a false account or e-mail address. Transferring copyrighted materials to or from the NITJ systems without the express consent of the owner is a violation of international law. In addition, the use of the internet for commercial gain or profit is not allowed from an educational site. If done so, it will be the sole responsibility of the user and the user has to face any legal consequences arising thereof on his/her own. The Institute will not be responsible for any such incident. Users must comply and adhere to the Digital Data Privacy and Protection Laws/Act. Downloading and installing any software has to be done with the explicit consent of the respective facility in-charges. Only authorized and Licensed software should be installed on computers/laptops, etc.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
Installation of unlicensed software on NITJ facilities, or on individual machines connected to the NITJ network, is strictly prohibited. If done so, it will be the sole responsibility of the user and the user has to face any legal consequences arising thereof on his/her own. The Institute will not be responsible for any such download/installation. Anti-Virus, Spyware software, OS, and Application Software should be kept up to date. Report suspicious emails, phishing attempts, or malware immediately to webmaster@nitj.ac.in. Setting up any facility requiring password transmission over clear text is prohibited. To the extent possible, users are expected to use their official email addresses provided by NIT Jalandhar for official communications and academic purposes only and for communication with other members of the Institute. Email content should be respectful, professional, and free of offensive content. It is forbidden to use electronic mail and other network communications facilities to harass, offend, or annoy other users of the network, including impeding their computing systems, software, or data. Chain letters are not allowed.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
Neither is any form of commercial advertising, or soliciting allowed. Spamming is strictly disallowed. Subscribing to mailing lists outside the Institute is an individual’s responsibility. Subscribing someone else to any group outside NIT Jalandhar is illegal. It is forbidden to send frivolous or academically unimportant messages to any group. Broadcast of messages to everyone in the system is allowed only for academic purposes and emergencies. Violations of this (as decided by concerned authorities) will result in immediate freezing of the user's account for an extended period, as determined by the authorities. Recreational downloads and peer-to-peer connections for recreational purposes are banned. Shared email accounts for any purpose whatsoever are not allowed. Any special accounts that need to be set up for conferences and other valid reasons, as determined by the institute authorities, must have a single designated user. To the extent possible, users are expected to connect only to the official NITJ Wi-Fi network for wireless access.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
Setting up of unsecured Wi-Fi systems on the NITJ network is prohibited in accordance with a Government of India ban. Use of VPNs and bypassing the firewall is strictly prohibited. VPNs may be used if explicitly approved by the IT Cell. Generative AI Tools may be used ethically for learning and idea generation but must not replace original academic work. Only Institute-approved Cloud Platforms should be used for academic work. Users are expected to take proper care of the equipment, and are expected to report any malfunction to the staff on duty or to the in charge of the facility. Users should not attempt to move, repair, reconfigure, modify, or attach external devices to the systems. NO FOOD OR DRINK is permitted in the laboratories. Smoking is strictly prohibited. Also, making noise either through games/ music or even talking and/ or singing loudly is prohibited. Playing Games in the Institute laboratories or using the Institute facilities is strictly prohibited. Internet chat is also banned.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
Display of offensive material (either on computer screens or through posters, etc.) is strictly disallowed, and serious action will be taken against offenders. Violations of policy will be treated as academic misconduct, misdemeanor, or indiscipline as appropriate. Depending upon the nature of the violation, the institute authorities may take action by issuing a warning through disabling the account. In extreme cases, the account may be completely deleted and/ or the user prohibited access to IT facilities at NITJ, and/ or sent to the Institute disciplinary action committee as constituted by the Institute authorities. The policy may change as and when it is considered appropriate, and new policies or changes in policy will take effect immediately after a brief announcement by any means, e-mail, printed notices, or through the news groups. Any unauthorized use of the Institute's digital resources, including but not limited to IP addresses, email accounts, and network infrastructure, is strictly prohibited. Individuals engaging in such activities shall be personally liable for any legal consequences arising therefrom.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
IT Infrastructure Usage Policy
The Institute disclaims all responsibility and shall not be held accountable for any misuse committed by individuals. Strict disciplinary and legal actions will be initiated against violators as per applicable laws and institutional regulations.
title: IT Infrastructure Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
title1: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
title2: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
desc: Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar Computer Centre Whom this Document Concerns All Users of IT infrastructure (Computers and the Network) at NIT, Jalandhar. Reason for Policy This policy outlines the responsible use of the Information Technology Infrastructure at NIT, Jalandhar. Statement of Policy All users of NIT, Jalandhar will be subject to the following Acceptable Use Policy 1. [Content] I shall be responsible for all use of this network.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
In case I own a computer and decide to connect it to NIT, Jalandhar network, I will be responsible for all the content on it, especially that which I make available to other users. (This provision will also apply to any computer or device for which I am responsible, and is included in the meaning of “my computer”.) In case I do not own a computer but am provided some IT resources by NIT, Jalandhar, I will be held responsible for the content stored in the designated workspace allotted to me (examples: file storage area, web pages, stored/archived emails, on Computer Centre or Department machines) 2. [Network] I will be held responsible for all the network traffic generated by “my computer”. I understand that network capacity is a limited, shared resource. I agree that physically tampering with network connections/equipment, sending disruptive signals, or making EXCESSIVE USE of network resources is strictly prohibited. Repeated offenses of this type could result in permanent disconnection of network services.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
I shall not share the network connection beyond my own use and will not act as a forwarder/ masquerader for anyone else. 3. [Academic Use] I understand that the IT infrastructure at NIT, Jalandhar, is for academic use and I shall not use it for any commercial purpose or to host data services for other people or groups. Also, I shall not host or broadcast information that might harm others or may be otherwise considered objectionable or illegal as per Indian law. I shall not use the Institute Logo, official mail ID on the social sites without prior permission from the competent authority. Further, I shall not air my grievances on the social sites/media and will approach the Institute Authority for the same. 4. [Identity] I shall not attempt to deceive others about my identity in electronic communications or network traffic. I will also not use NIT, Jalandhar IT resources to threaten, intimidate, or harass others. 5. [Privacy] I will not intrude on the privacy of anyone.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
In particular, I will not try to access computers (hacking), accounts, files, or information belonging to others without their knowledge and explicit consent. 6. [Monitoring] I understand that the IT resources provided to me are subject to monitoring, with cause, as determined through consultation with the NIT, Jalandhar administration, when applicable. The monitoring may include aggregate bandwidth usage to effectively manage limited IT resources, as well as monitoring traffic content in response to a legal or law enforcement request to do so. I authorize NIT, Jalandhar administration to perform network vulnerability and port scans on my systems, as needed, for protecting the overall integrity and efficiency of the NIT, Jalandhar network. 7. [Viruses] I shall maintain my computer on this network with current virus detection software and current updates of my operating system, and I shall attempt to keep my computer free from viruses, worms, Trojans, and other similar programs.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
8. [File Sharing] I shall not use the IT infrastructure to engage in any form of illegal file sharing (examples: copyrighted material, obscene material). In particular, I have noted the following: Electronic resources such as e-journals, e-books, databases, etc. made available by the Central Library, NIT, Jalandhar are for academic use. These resources can be searched, browsed, and material may be downloaded and printed as single copies of articles as is done in the case of printed library material. Downloading or printing of a complete book or an entire issue, or a volume of one or more journals (called systematic downloading) is strictly prohibited. Use of robots, spiders or intelligent agents to access, search and / or systematically download from the e-resources is also prohibited. Any violation of this policy will result in penal action as per the rules and regulations of the Institute. I am aware that Systematic downloading will result in the publisher blocking the entire community of users at NIT, Jalandhar, from accessing these resources.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
9. [Security] I understand that I will not take any steps that endanger the security of the NIT, Jalandhar network. Specifically, I will not attempt to bypass firewalls and access rules in place. This includes not setting up servers of any kind (examples: web, mail, proxy) that are visible to the world outside the NIT, Jalandhar campus. In critical situations, NIT, Jalandhar authorities reserve the right to disconnect any device or disable any account if they believe that either is involved in compromising the information security of NIT, Jalandhar." 10. [Penalties] I understand that any use of IT infrastructure at NIT, Jalandhar that constitutes a violation of NIT, Jalandhar Regulations could result in administrative or disciplinary procedures. If I violate any of the above or any other act which is against the interest of the Institute/Society at large, I shall be liable for any major or minor penalty as deemed fit by the competent authority, and any ramifications arising thereof will be my sole responsibility.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

text:
Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy
The Institute will not be held responsible /accountable for any punitive/legal action arising thereof. I have read and understood the IT policy of the institute and agree to it wholeheartedly. I also agree and understand that the Institute disclaims all responsibility and shall not be held accountable for any misuse committed by individuals.
title: Undertaking with respect to NITJ IT Usage Policy

Cyber Volunteer Programme
title1: Cyber Volunteer Programme
title2: Step-by-Step Procedure for Registration of Volunteers in Cyber Volunteer Programme of the Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. Of India.
desc: To register on National Cybercrime Reporting Portal as Cyber Volunteer. Go to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal website cybercrime.gov.in . Under Cyber Volunteer Menu, Select "Register As A Volunteer" option. Read the Process of Registion to register on Portal, Create ‘Login Id’. Mention name of State/UT of your Residence and Mobile Number which are mandatory. Enter OTP received on your mobile on ‘Login Id’ page and ‘submit’. Provide the required information in “Registration Step 1” on page “USER VOLUNTEER PROFILE DETAILS”. Further, Upload resume, ID Proof, Address Proof and Passport size photograph. It is at this step you have to Select Type of Volunteership:- – Cyber Volunteer Unlawful Content Flagger – Cyber Awareness Promoter – Cyber Expert.
title: Cyber Volunteer Programme

text:
Cyber Volunteer Programme
In ‘Registration Step 2’, mention the reason to be a Cyber Volunteer, including other details, skillset etc. ‘Save and continue’ to come to “Preview and Final Submit”. In “Preview and Final Submit”, recheck the details again before clicking “Final Submit”. For registration as ‘Cyber Awareness Promoter or Cyber Expert’, prior verification (KYC) will be carried out. To check the status of registration, go to “View Profile” Applicable ID and Address proof required to be uploaded. ID proof i.e. Aadhar Card/Indian Passport/Voter ID card/PAN Card/Driving license Residence proof i.e. Indian Passport/Voter ID card/ Electricity Bill (not older than 3 months)/Domicile Certificate with photo of the addressee.
title: Cyber Volunteer Programme

desc: Dr. B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar is celebrating the Engineer's Day on 15 th September 2023 . On this occasion, poster presentations, project/experiment demonstration and logo competition will be organized in the institute. The details of events are given below. (i) Poster should be based on the research/project work of the student. Best poster from each department will be selected for the award. Hard copy of poster should be of suitable size so that it is clearly visible to the evaluator/audience. (ii) Best project/experiment demonstrations will also be awarded (iii) Logo competition is based on the theme "Space mission of India". Best logo will be selected and awarded. Note: Students participating in logo competition are requested to submit their self-designed/created logo on or before 14th September 2023 in the office of Physics department with their name, roll number and contact details clearly mentioned on the hard copy (of the clearly visible logo).

title1: Technology Business Incubator (TBI)
title2: Technology Business Incubator (TBI)
desc: Technology Business Incubator (TBI) has been established at Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar with the support of Department of Science and Technology. TBI has been registered as a Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 with the name ‘NITJ Technology Business Incubator’. NITJ Technology Business Incubator has a separate Board of Governors for laying down the policies and procedures so as to govern the activities for better working towards achieving its objectives. Website: https://www.nitj.ac.in/tbi Policy and Procedures for NITJ Technology Business Incubator Call for Innovative Startups on 10th November 2023 Startup India Seed Fund Scheme ROUND 3 Objectives of NITJ Technology Business Incubator: To setup a vibrant startup ecosystem so as to align itself with our country’s major policy initiatives of Make in India and Start-up India; Stand-up India. To set up incubator facilities, provide cost effective infrastructural support and value added services to startups like mentoring, legal, financial, technical, intellectual property related.
title: Technology Business Incubator (TBI)

text:
Technology Business Incubator (TBI)
To support NITJ in creating a platform to nurture creativity, innovation and entrepreneurial skills of faculty and students. To provide a platform for speedy commercialization of technologies developed by NITJ or by any other academic/technical/R&D institution or by an individual. To build a close and pragmatic collaboration between the educational institutions, research institutions, management institutions on the one hand and industry and other user organisations on the other. To facilitate the dissemination of information by organising conferences, seminars, lecture series, workshops and boot-camps, hackathons etc. To generally do and perform all the above acts and such other things as may be deemed incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects or of any of them or any allied objects or which may advantageously or conveniently be combined with the programme of the Society in a profitable way.
title: Technology Business Incubator (TBI)

title1: TEST
title2: TEST
desc: The alumni meet held at NIT JALANDHAR on December 16, 2023, was a poignant occasion that evoked a strong sense of nostalgia among the attendees. This annual gathering, cherished by both former and current members of the NITJ community, serves a dual purpose. On one hand, it rekindles connections among alumni, allowing them to celebrate shared successes and achievements and also it provides a valuable platform for current students to engage with distinguished alumni, gaining insights across diverse professional fields. The event became a momentous occasion as alumni from various walks of life credited their accomplishments, whether in business, entrepreneurship, or administration, to the guidance they received from the professors during their time at NITJ. The impact of these mentors was acknowledged and appreciated, creating a deep sense of gratitude among the alumni. The significance of each department was highlighted through the honoring of outstanding alumni, each of whom received recognition for their contributions.
title: The alumni meet held at NIT JALANDHAR on

text:
The alumni meet held at NIT JALANDHAR on
In their heartfelt acceptance speeches, these individuals expressed sincere thanks to the institute for playing a pivotal role in shaping their journeys. Beyond recognition, the meet also became a platform for giving back. Mr. Rohit Khanna, a 1994 passout, sponsored scholarships for 20 deserving students from various departments. This gesture not only supports the academic pursuits of current students but also exemplifies the spirit of alumni support. A notable aspect of the event was the gathering of 85 alumni, spanning regions across the country and even reaching beyond borders. This diverse group pledged to contribute to the institute's legacy by establishing a special, well-furnished room for the Alumni House.
title: The alumni meet held at NIT JALANDHAR on

desc: Dear Students, This is regarding allotment of Open Elective course for B.Tech 7th semester (July-Dec, 2024 session). You are required to fill the Online "Open Elective Allotment" Form by login to your NITJ ERP account: https://nitj.ac.in/erp/login The choices are available in the drop-down menu and the detailed syllabi of Open Elective courses are given below so as to help you choose the appropriate Elective: List of Open Elective Courses Syllabus of Open Elective Courses You must submit the Form by May 8, 2024, failing which you will not get the OE course of your choice. You are required to ensure that YOU HAVE NOT STUDIED THE OPTED COURSE IN YOUR B TECH PROGRAMME EARLIER, i.e. upto 6th semester. In case of repeated course/contents, credits earned through this course shall not be considered.
title: Open Elective Allotment

text:
Open Elective Allotment
The following guidelines have been followed for the allotment process: The students from a particular department cannot opt for the course being offered by their own department (e.g. students of ECE department cannot opt for the courses being offered by the ECE department). Students of IT and CSE departments cannot opt for the courses being offered by both these departments.

Non-GATE candidates shall be admitted based upon the entrance test to be carried out by the respective department(s). title1: Integrated B.Tech - Mba
title2: Integrated B.Tech - MBA Program (IBM) with IIM Amritsar
desc: Integrated B.Tech. – MBA Program (IBM) is being jointly offered by IIM Amritsar and NIT Jalandhar. The program will integrate the curriculum of B.Tech. degree from NIT Jalandhar and MBA degree from IIM Amritsar in 5 years, thereby saving one academic year for the students. Admission to the program will be through an entrance test conducted by IIM Amritsar followed by a Personal Interview. All 4th semester students of NIT Jalandhar are eligible to apply for the program. The first year MBA curriculum will be covered in semesters 5-8 of the B.Tech. program. Students will also get an opportunity to do summer internships in managerial roles at the end of 8th semester. The IBM program offers B.Tech. students of NIT Jalandhar a unique opportunity to be corporate ready with this Integrated B.Tech. MBA degree. More details are available here - https://iimamritsar.ac.in/p/about-program-5
title: Integrated B.Tech - Mba

Celebrating Our Alumnus
title1: Celebrating Our Alumnus
title2: Celebrating Our Alumnus: Prince Kumar Singh 's Remarkable Achievement
desc: We are thrilled to share the exciting news that our esteemed alumnus, Mr. Prince Kumar Singh Batch of 2016-2020), has achieved an extraordinary milestone AIR15 by qualifying for the prestigious UPSC Indian Forest Service (IFS) exam . The UPSC IFS exam is known for its rigorous selection process and is one of the most challenging examinations in India. Mr.Prince's success in this exam is a testament to his dedication, hard work, and exceptional intellect. This accomplishment is not only a personal triumph but also a moment of immense pride for all of us at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar . Mr Prince Kumar Singh has always been a beacon of excellence, demonstrating an unwavering commitment to academic and professional pursuits. This latest achievement further cements his/her status as a role model for our current students and fellow alumni.
title: Celebrating Our Alumnus

text:
Celebrating Our Alumnus
We had the opportunity to catch up with Mr Prince Kumar Singh following this significant achievement, and here is what he had to say: " I'm Prince Kumar Singh, B.Tech Chemical Engineering ( Batch 2016-2020). Those four years were the best part of my life. NITJ blessed me with good friends from different parts of the country. I got good exposure and a conducive environment here. I learned so many things from friends and professors, due to which I scored the highest marks in chemical engineering optional in the history of IFS exam as per my knowledge. Apart from Academics, I was also a member of the library committee and PRAYAAS society. PRAYAAS society provided me with an opportunity to teach children from the poor section of society who can't afford to send their children to good schools. Being from a lower middle class family, I could easily relate with the financial constraints that one faces in life.
title: Celebrating Our Alumnus

text:
Celebrating Our Alumnus
The hard work for the betterment of others will always keep me motivated to bring positive change to the lives of poor people. Even today, I miss the beautiful campus, classes, hostel life, cultural and technical fests, hanging out with my peer groups, and the whole family of NITJians. The values like integrity, compassion, perseverance and self-discipline which I learned here will remain forever and will always motivate me to serve the nation to the best of my abilities. As Mr Prince Kumar Singh embarks on this new and exciting chapter, we are confident that he will make significant contributions to the field of forestry and environmental conservation. We look forward to following his journey and celebrating future accomplishments. Please join us in congratulating Mr Prince Kumar Singh on this remarkable achievement! His success is an inspiration to us all and a reminder of the incredible potential within the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar community.
title: Celebrating Our Alumnus

desc: National Innovation and Startup Policy (NISP) Dr B R Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar Home Vision Mission Objectives Activities Members NISP Policy National Innovation and Startup Policy (NISP): NIT Jalandhar wants to be the hub of Innovation and Entrepreneurship in the whole of Punjab. In order to achieve the vision, NIT Jalandhar has drafted an Innovation and Startup Policy that will act as a framework and guiding force for all the stakeholders in their endeavor on I&E related activities. This Innovation and Startup Policy enlists all the rules related to I&E activities, startups, teachings and sessions of entrepreneurship, innovation workshops, events and IPR. This policy will enforce every stakeholder to abide by it in case of any discrepancy. The policy is binding in nature. The aim of the policy is to encourage every stakeholder at NIT Jalandhar and the Technology Business Incubator to take up innovation, entrepreneurship and startups as core activities so that NIT Jalandhar in itself grows to be self-sufficient in the future.
title: NISP

text:
NISP
Due focus is put on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and financial independence so that students graduate from NIT Jalandhar not just as engineers but as concerned citizens who give due regard to the environment and the society they live in. This policy will ensure that the students focus more on product development and product management rather than theories which in turn will ensure that the host institute will file more IPRs and go for more startups and Technology Transfers. This policy aligns itself with the National Innovation and Startup Policy and with the constitution of NIT Jalandhar Vision To make NIT Jalandhar the hub of innovation and entrepreneurship with world class support so that the students graduate from here with expertise in innovative product making and entrepreneurship. Mission To promote grassroots innovation on the campus Encourage students, faculty and staff to come with new ideas and product designs Make it a norm for all students to design, develop and manage new products.
title: NISP

text:
NISP
File 200 IPRs per year so that 150+ IPRs are granted per year. Encourage final year students to take up product development as their final year project in a group of 6 students Encourage faculty, staff and students to start up. Encourage all staying on the campus to think of financial independence and work on it. text:
I -STEM
title1: I -STEM
title2: The Indian Science, Technology and Engineering Facilities Map (I-STEM)
desc: This interactive web portal is designed to accelerate scientific advancement across India by providing comprehensive access to a wide range of scientific infrastructure and research facilities. Key Objectives of I-STEM: Building a National R&D Infrastructure Network: I-STEM establishes a digital platform for listing and sharing major R&D equipment and facilities, fostering collaboration and resource optimization among academic institutions, research labs, and industries. Cultivating a Culture of Innovation: The platform promotes a culture of sharing and knowledge exchange, helping translate ideas into tangible products and advancements, thereby enhancing the overall quality of research. Enhancing Indigenous R&D Capacity: By connecting academic and industrial R&D labs, I-STEM empowers researchers to build indigenous capacity and expertise, promoting self-reliance in critical scientific domains. Boosting Industry & Startup Innovation: I-STEM fosters R&D and innovation within industries and startups, encouraging the development and manufacturing of essential devices and instruments, which are crucial for India’s technological growth.
title: I -STEM

text:
I -STEM
Optimizing Resource Utilization: The portal ensures the optimal utilization of publicly funded resources and technology, maximizing their impact on research efforts and reducing redundancy in investments. Key Features of I-STEM: Access to Facilities: I-STEM provides information about scientific equipment and research facilities available at various academic institutions, R&D labs, and private industries across India, enabling researchers to identify and utilize resources that are otherwise inaccessible. Booking and Utilization: Researchers can directly book time slots for using specific equipment through the portal, thereby facilitating more efficient research workflows. Collaborations and Networking: The platform promotes interdisciplinary collaborations by connecting researchers with facilities and experts in various fields, fostering a spirit of innovation and problem-solving. Funding Opportunities and Announcements: The portal also keeps users updated about the latest announcements regarding funding opportunities, fellowships, and other research support initiatives. Benefits to Our Research Community: Enhanced Research Quality: Utilize state-of-the-art facilities to elevate the quality of your research outputs. Cost-Efficient Research: Access to shared resources reduces the financial burden of acquiring expensive equipment.
title: I -STEM

text:
I -STEM
Accelerated Progress: With easy access to necessary tools and collaborations, your research timelines can be significantly shortened. How to Get Started: Visit the I-STEM portal at https://www.istem.gov.in . Register as a user to explore available facilities. Search for specific equipment or facilities relevant to your research. Make bookings as per the availability and requirements of your research work.
title: I -STEM

desc: SPORTS AND HEALTHCARE RESEARCH CENTRE Preamble The Sports and Healthcare Research Centre focuses on advancing knowledge and innovation at the crossroads of sports science and healthcare. The main aim is to nurture research that aids in developing new sports materials and devices with engineering art for improving human healthcare. The centre would pursue research on fitness standards, physical training, and healthcare among all common individuals and sportspersons. The centre will also focus on the environment connected to human health. Our mission is to improve athletic performance while supporting overall health and well-being.
title: OLD - SPORTS AND HEALTHCARE RESEARCH CENTRE

text:
GATE - 2 0 2 5
title1: GATE - 2 0 2 5
desc: Abhay Singh Secures AIR 1 in the country, Over 70 Students Achieve Top Ranks Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar has demonstrated exceptional academic excellence in the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) 2025. Leading this achievement is Abhay Singh, a Civil Engineering graduate, who secured All India Rank (AIR) 1, a remarkable leap from his previous AIR 1659 in 2024. Hailing from Chandauli, Uttar Pradesh, Abhay completed his B.Tech in Civil Engineering at NIT Jalandhar. He dedicated himself to preparation of GATE, the Indian Engineering Services (IES), and the Civil Services Examination under the guidance of his professors in the Department of Civil Engineering. He attributes his success to a solid grasp of fundamental concepts, the unwavering support of his family, and the mentorship of his professors, particularly Prof. S.P. Singh, under whose guidance he completed his final-year project. Beyond Abhay's outstanding performance, NIT Jalandhar celebrates the success of over 70 students from all the engineering departments of the institute who qualified in GATE 2025.
title: GATE - 2 0 2 5

text:
GATE - 2 0 2 5
Impressively, 9 students secured ranks within top 50, more than 12 students secured ranks within top 100, and 25 students ranked under 500, underscoring the institute's commitment to fostering academic excellence and competitive exam readiness. Prof. B.K. Kanaujia, Director of Dr B R Ambedkar NIT Jalandhar, extended heartfelt congratulations to Abhay and all successful students. He also acknowledged the dedicated efforts of the faculty members, reaffirming the institute's role in shaping future leaders in engineering and public service. The GATE is highly important for B.Tech students, as it opens numerous academic and career opportunities. It is the primary exam for admission to IITs, NITs, IIITs, and other top engineering institutes for master's programs as well as PhD programmes. Further, many Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) recruit engineers directly through GATE score with high-paying jobs. While some international universities also consider GATE scores for admission, this exam is the gateway for opportunities in esteemed research institutions such as DRDO, ISRO etc.
title: GATE - 2 0 2 5

text:
GATE - 2 0 2 5
NIT Jalandhar's comprehensively designed curriculum is strategically aligned with GATE, providing students with a strong conceptual foundation and competitive edge to secure top ranks. In addition to academic achievements, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar NIT Jalandhar achieved an 87% placement rate in 2023-2024, with 700 B.Tech students placed out of 811 eligible candidates. The highest package was ₹52 LPA, with an average of ₹9.48 LPA. Over 220 recruiters, including KPMG, Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Texas Instruments, BPCL, and Adani Group, participated, highlighting the institute’s strong industry ties. With outstanding academics and placements, NIT Jalandhar continues to excel in engineering education and career development.
title2: NIT Jalandhar Shines in GATE 2025
title: GATE - 2 0 2 5

desc: The Department of Electrical Engineering is delighted to announce that Mr. Mrityunjay Tiwari (Roll No. 23126035) has been awarded the "Renu Mittal EE Merit Scholarship" for achieving the highest CGPA in the first two semesters of the 2023 batch EE students. This merit-based scholarship, sponsored annually by our esteemed alumnus Mr. Bhavya Mittal, provides a financial reward of ₹10,000/- to recognize and celebrate academic excellence. The award ceremony was graced by the presence of the Dean of Student Welfare (DSW), the Head of the Department of Electrical Engineering, and faculty members. We extend our heartfelt congratulations to Mr. Mrityunjay Tiwari for this achievement and express our sincere gratitude to Mr. Bhavya Mittal for his continued support in shaping the future of engineering students.

title1: Alumni Lecture
title2: Alumni Lecture by Mr. Vipul Sharma, a Distinguished Alumnus from B.Tech (Batch-2009)
desc: The department had the privilege of hosting an insightful alumni lecture delivered on 13th August 2025 by Mr. Vipul Sharma, a distinguished alumnus from the B.Tech (Batch-2009). Currently working in the field of supply chain management, Mr. Sharma engaged with the 3rd and final year B.Tech students, sharing valuable industry knowledge and personal experiences. During the session, he shed light on key aspects of supply chain operations, emerging trends, and the growing importance of this field in today's global economy. His practical insights helped bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world applications. Students had the opportunity to interact directly with Mr. Sharma, ask questions, and gain clarity on various career pathways within the supply chain domain. The session proved to be highly informative and motivating, leaving the students with a clearer understanding of the opportunities and challenges in the supply chain industry.
title: Alumni Lecture

text:
Guest Lecture
title1: Guest Lecture
title2: Inspiring Guest Lecture by Dr. Rohit Arora, an alumnus of Batch-2014
desc: The department had the pleasure of hosting Dr. Rohit Arora, an accomplished Operations Research Scientist and proud alumnus of the Batch-2014, for an inspiring guest lecture on 14th August 2025. Currently based in Bangalore, Dr. Arora holds a Ph.D. from the University of British Columbia (UBC), British Columbia, and has made significant contributions in the field of operations research. During his session, Dr. Arora shared his personal and professional journey — from his undergraduate days to pursuing a doctorate abroad — providing students with a realistic and motivating perspective on academic growth, research challenges, and international opportunities. He emphasized the importance of clarity of purpose, persistence, and critical thinking, along with cultivating strong foundations in mathematics, data analytics, and programming. He also advised students to remain open to interdisciplinary learning, be proactive in seeking research or internship experiences, and to not shy away from stepping out of their comfort zones.
title: Guest Lecture

text:
Guest Lecture
The session concluded with an engaging Q&A, leaving the students inspired and better informed about the path ahead in both higher education and research-driven careers.

Aarogya Club Launches 'NITJ का अपना Blood Bank Platform' - A Student-Driven Initiative
title2: Aarogya Club Launches 'NITJ का अपना Blood Bank Platform' - A Student-Driven Initiative
desc: The Aarogya Club of NIT Jalandhar has launched NITJ का अपना Blood Bank Platform, a first-of-its-kind, student-driven initiative to provide timely, transparent, and trustworthy support during blood emergencies. In moments of crisis, families often struggle through informal WhatsApp groups to find donors—facing delays, lack of trust, and no structured system. To solve this, Aarogya Club has created a dedicated platform where blood requests can be raised instantly and fulfilled by verified student donors. This initiative has been developed under the visionary leadership of Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia (Director, NITJ), Prof. Ajay Bansal (Registrar), Prof. Rohit Mehra (Dean, Research & Consultancy), and Prof. Anish Kumar Sachdeva (Dean, Student Welfare), with the guidance and support of Dr. Tarun Sehgal (Medical Officer & Faculty Coordinator, Aarogya Club) and Dr. Ravi Verma (Faculty Coordinator, Aarogya Club). How it Works: Anyone in need can submit a request through the official Blood Request Form. Aarogya Club contacts matching registered donors from the NITJ community. Verified student donors step up to ensure timely support.
title: Aarogya Club Launches 'NITJ का अपना Blood Bank Platform' - A Student-Driven Initiative

text:
NIT Jalandhar's 20 Faculty Members Featured Among World’s Top 2% Scientists
title2: NIT Jalandhar's 20 Faculty Members Featured Among World’s Top 2% Scientists
desc: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology, Jalandhar, has once again brought laurels at the global level. As per the list of the Top 2% Scientists in the World, 20 faculty members of the institute, including Director Prof. B. K. Kanaujia, have been featured among the world’s leading scientists. This prestigious list, compiled by Stanford University in collaboration with Elsevier, is considered one of the most credible assessments of scientific research impact worldwide. It evaluates scientists across 22 broad fields and 174 sub-fields using a composite indicator that accounts for research productivity, citations, h-index, co-authorship, and author position. Scientists are recognized both for career-long impact and for contributions in the most recent year, reflecting their sustained excellence and global influence. The recognition underscores NIT Jalandhar’s academic and research excellence across key areas, including Engineering, Technology, Applied Sciences, Biotechnology, Environmental Sciences, and Materials Science. The faculty members recognized in this global ranking are Prof. Binod Kumar Kanaujia (Director), along with Prof. Vishal S. Sharma, Prof. Balbir Singh Kaith, Prof.
title: NIT Jalandhar's 20 Faculty Members Featured Among World’s Top 2% Scientists

text:
Mr. Akash Kumar has secured AIR-789 in UPSC 2025
title2: Mr. Akash Kumar has secured AIR-789 in UPSC 2025
desc: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jalandhar proudly celebrates the success of its alumnus Mr. Akash Kumar (Mechanical Engineering, Batch 2017–2021) , who has secured All India Rank (AIR) 789 in the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2025 . After completing his B.Tech from NIT Jalandhar, Akash Kumar secured a campus placement at Larsen & Toubro . However, driven by his aspiration to serve the nation through the Civil Services, he left the job after working there for a brief period and dedicated himself fully to UPSC preparation. Despite facing challenges during his journey, his perseverance, resilience, and determination ultimately led to this remarkable achievement. His inspiring journey reflects the power of dedication and hard work and serves as a motivation for students and aspirants across the country. The NIT Jalandhar fraternity extends heartfelt congratulations to him and wishes him great success in his journey of public service.
title: Mr. Akash Kumar has secured AIR-789 in UPSC 2025

text:
Hostels
The students who wish to stay with their parents or guardians outside the campus for short period may be allowed to do so with the permission of the competent authority. Hostel wardens are appointed for each hostel and they exercise 'general supervision' and 'control' over the inmates. Hostel attendants are available round the clock in hostel. In case of any problem related to the hostel, the student should contact/meet the attendant. In case of illness or medical emergency hostel resident should inform to the concerned warden through hostel staff. Possessing any kind of motorized vehicle, e.g. car, scooter, motorcycle, moped etc. by the hostlers is not permitted. Any hostler is allowed to go to his/her home (only) during vacations/weekends against intimation to the hostel office. It is mandatory to fill the hostel leave form and submit to the security guard at hostel gate. Institute does not own the responsibility of theft and loss of any items possessed by the inmates (like laptop, mobile phone, tablet etc).
title: Hostels

text:
Hostels
However, in the interest of inmates it is advised here that they may get insured their valuables. All hostlers are required to observe the hostel timings strictly. The gate timings of the hostels are decided by the competent authority from time to time. In case of un-avoidable circumstances students shall have to take special permission in advance from the concerned warden to stay out for late hours. For any kind of meeting in hostel premise, prior written permission/approval is mandatory from the competent authority. The students shall make proper use of common rooms having newspapers, literature and other articles meant for indoor games. The hostel warden will fix hours of the common room from time to time. Hostel Rules Disciplinary Rules:- No student should be in possession of fire-arm, lethal weapon, alcohol or drugs, poisonous thing or intoxicant of any kind in the hostel.

Debarring from representing the institution in any national or international meet, tournament, youth festival, conference etc. Suspension/expulsion from the hostel. Rustication from the institution. Expulsion from the institution and consequent debarring from admission in other institutions. Fine up to Rs. 50,000/- Collective punishment will be awarded if the individuals committing indiscipline are not identified. Room Allotment Rules:- The student must be personally present at the time of allotment of rooms and he/she may be allowed to choose his/her roommates. Every boarder will be responsible for the items issued to them. Furniture and electrical fittings are not to be moved from one room to another.
title: Hostels

text:
Hostels
All the boarders shall vacate the hostel rooms before they leave for vacation so that annual repairs/maintenance and white washing etc may be carried out. All the hostel room articles issued (at the time of room allotment) to the students will be returned/ surrendered to the hostel staff/attendant/clerk before leaving the hostel during or at the end of the session. The room occupants will be responsible for any loss or damage to the items issued to him/her (at the time of room allotment) and the same will be recovered from them as decided by the competent authority. No boarder is allowed to change his/her room without the permission of the Warden and shall have to vacate accommodation as and when asked for. Each room occupant should lock his/her room. Any room found unlocked due to the negligence of the student/resident will be charged fine as decided by competent authority. Mess Rules:- The messes of all hostels operate on cooperative basis.
title: Hostels

text:
Hostels
A committee of the students from every hostel manages the affairs of the mess under the supervision of wardens. While visiting the dining hall, the common room and canteen, the students should be in their proper dress. All hostel inmates are required to follow the norms of the hostel/mess and required to deposit the mess advance (mess charges, maintenance charges, extra meal charges, service charges etc) as decided from time to time in each semester by the hostel authorities for availing mess facility. Minimum 55 diets are mandatory for every hostel resident. The remaining balance of mess advance (if any) will be refunded after one year or the student leaves hostel whichever is earlier. Wastage of food is strictly prohibited; the same may be liable to charging of fine as decided by the competent authority. Student's Guest Rule:- No outsider is allowed to stay in the hostel. However any relative/guest of the student may be allowed with prior permission of the competent authority.
title: Hostels

text:
Hostels
The permissible guests include father/ brother and mother/sister (in case of girl students) provided he/she comes from a far off place. Female guests are not permitted to stay in boys' hostel. Likewise male guests are not permitted to stay in the girls' hostel. A boarder keeping a guest without the prior permission of the Warden is liable to be penalized. Students/room occupants are not allowed to stay/sleep in the room of fellow student during daytime/night even with his/her consent. Withdrawal/Expulsion from the Hostels:- After the general allotment, application for withdrawal from the hostel should be counter-signed by the father/guardian and submitted to the hostel warden. It should also be ensured that the student does not owe any hostel dues. The Director/ DSW/ Chief Warden may expel a boarder from the hostel, if he/she is in the habit of staying away without intimation to the hostel office, or hostel fee and mess dues are not cleared in time.
title: Hostels

text:
Hostels
Students who do not clear their dues, such as dues of the hostel mess, canteen, fine etc. by the prescribed date will not be registered for the subsequent semester until and unless, they clear all their dues and submit "No Dues Certificate" from the Account Section and the concerned hostel warden. The students who leave the Institute after completing the degree requirements or otherwise, their result as well as the provisional certificate/ degree will be withheld till NO DUE CERTIFICATE is produced. No boarder shall leave the hostel without handing over the charge of the room as per the inventory issued at the time of allotment. Hostel Guest Rooms Some hostel has a guest room with basic amenities that can be booked by students for their parents through hostel clerk on the recommendation of warden of the hostel.

text:
Fee Structure and Instructions for Online Fee Payment and Semester Registration (B.Tech 2nd Semester)
For any Technical Difficulty, Contact at Email: webmaster@nitj.ac.in Important Instructions: All B.Tech. students who want to claim a waiver of the Tuition Fee shall be required to submit the latest Income Certificate issued by the appropriate authority on or after 01.04.2022 (The option to Upload Income Certificate is available in the Fee Portal ) The Students studying through Education Loan have to upload the Letter issued by the Concerned Bank Branch Manager as per the format/instructions mentioned in the Fee Structure. (The option to Upload Bank Letter is available in the Registration Portal ) The Students who are studying through Education Loan, If also claiming Tuition Fee waiver based on Income, they have to merge the Bank Letter and Income Certificate into a Single PDF file and upload on the Registration Portal. Don't use the direct link of any Bank for Semester Fee Payment, Fee must be paid only through NITJ Fee Portal. Payment through Demand Draft / Internet Transfer directly to the Institute account will not be entertained.
title: Fee Structure and Instructions for Online Fee Payment and Semester Registration (B.Tech 2nd Semester)

text:
Fee Structure and Instructions for Online Fee Payment and Semester Registration (B.Tech 2nd Semester)
After Successful Transaction, Download PDF of e-Receipt from NITJ Fee Portal. During Fee Payment, If the amount is debited from your bank account, and Fee Status has not been updated on the NITJ Fee Portal. You can contact at email: webmaster@nitj.ac.in Note: If you are using Debit/Credit Card for Fee Payment, Transaction Failure may be occurred due to the following reason: Your Card has a restriction on the maximum amount you can withdraw at a time. In this case, Please use the following option(s): Option 1: Use NetBanking Option 2: Use Another Card that has a withdrawal limit more than the amount to be paid. Option 3: You can also make payment through Challan, For this, please follow the below steps: 1. Login to NITJ Fee Portal, Select ICICI payment gateway. 2. In the Next Screen, click on Make Payment Button. 3. In the Next Screen, Select NEFT/RTGS option. 4. Click on Generate Challan Button. 5.

text:
Alumni Expert Talk by Mr. Ajith Mohan Karimpana, Founder & CEO of Furlenco, on 2nd September 2025
title: Alumni Expert Talk by Mr. Ajith Mohan Karimpana, Founder & CEO of Furlenco, on 2nd September 2025
desc: From Campus to Crores – The Success Story of our Alumnus, Mr. Ajith Mohan Karimpana We are delighted to invite you to an Inspirational Talk featuring our distinguished alumnus Mr. Ajith Mohan Karimpana, the Founder and CEO of Furlenco, one of India’s leading furniture rental companies. Mr. Karimpana’s journey from NIT Jalandhar to building a company (Furlenco) with a turnover of ₹400 crore is a true inspiration for aspiring entrepreneurs. Today, Furlenco has grown into a large organization with more than 300 employees working under his leadership. In this session, he will share his experiences, challenges, and learnings from the entrepreneurial world — providing valuable insights on innovation, perseverance, and scaling a startup from scratch. Details of the Event: Date: 02 September 2025 Time: 4:00 PM Location: Virtual Mode (YouTube) YouTube Link: https://www.youtube.com/live/8ue7lvGL8ds?si=oHxabMo2mAN3njBn This is an excellent opportunity for you to interact with and learn from one of our most accomplished alumnus. We encourage everyone to attend the session and make the most of this enriching experience
title: Alumni Expert Talk by Mr. Ajith Mohan Karimpana, Founder & CEO of Furlenco, on 2nd September 2025
